docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Q: Why an extension instead of just a userscript? A: Userscripts are blocked by CSP on many important sites (GitHub, Gmail, banking). Extensions have elevated privileges and can bypass CSP.

Q: Is it safe to bypass CSP? A: Yes! Browser extensions are designed to have elevated privileges. CSP restrictions apply to web content, not to trusted browser extensions.

Q: Why Manifest V2? A: Chrome is phasing out Manifest V2 extensions. Manifest V2 is the future-proof standard for Chrome extensions.

Q: Will this work on Edge, Brave, or other Chromium browsers? A: Yes! This extension should work on any Chromium-based browser (Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi, etc.). Just load it in developer mode.

Q: Can I use both userscript and extension? A: It's recommended to use only one at a time to avoid conflicts. The extension is the better choice for compatibility.

Q: When will it be on Chrome Web Store? A: We're preparing for submission! See CHROME_WEB_STORE.md for our publication roadmap and how you can help.

docs.title: Permanent Installation Guide
docs.text: This guide explains how to install the Inspekt extension permanently in Firefox.

docs.title: Quick Answer
docs.text:
For regular Firefox users: The easiest way is to reload the temporary extension each time you restart Firefox (Method 1 below). We're working on submitting to the Firefox Add-ons store for one-click permanent installation.

For developers: Use Firefox Developer Edition with unsigned extensions enabled (Method 2 below).

docs.title: Method 1: Temporary Installation (Easiest)
docs.text:
Pros: - No special setup required - Works with regular Firefox - Perfect for testing and development

Cons: - Needs to be reloaded after Firefox restarts

docs.title: Steps:
docs.text:
1. Navigate to about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox
  2. Click "Load Temporary Add-on..."
  3. Select manifest.json from the extensions/firefox/ directory

Note: You'll need to repeat these steps each time you restart Firefox.

docs.title: Method 2: Self-Hosted Unsigned Extension (Developer Edition/Nightly)
docs.text:
Pros: - Permanent installation - No signing required - Full control

Cons: - Requires Firefox Developer Edition or Nightly - Need to disable signature verification

docs.title: 2.1 Install Firefox Developer Edition or Nightly
docs.text: Download one of these: - Firefox Developer Edition: https://www.mozilla.org/firefox/developer/ - Firefox Nightly: https://www.mozilla.org/firefox/nightly/

docs.title: 2.2 Build the Extension
docs.text:
cd extensions/firefox
./build.sh

This creates build/zen-browser-bridge-4.0.0.xpi

docs.title: 2.3 Disable Signature Verification
docs.text:
1. Open Firefox Developer Edition/Nightly
  2. Navigate to about:config
  3. Accept the risk warning
  4. Search for xpinstall.signatures.required
  5. Set it to false (double-click to toggle)

docs.title: 2.4 Install the Extension
docs.text:
Option A: Drag and Drop 1. Open Firefox 2. Drag build/zen-browser-bridge-4.0.0.xpi into Firefox window 3. Click "Add" when prompted

Option B: File Picker 1. Navigate to about:addons 2. Click the gear icon (⚙️) 3. Select "Install Add-on From File..." 4. Choose build/zen-browser-bridge-4.0.0.xpi 5. Click "Add" when prompted

The extension is now permanently installed!

docs.title: Method 3: Web Extension Signing (Recommended for Distribution)
docs.text:
Pros: - Works with regular Firefox - Permanent installation - Can be shared with others - Most secure method

Cons: - Requires Mozilla Developer account - Takes time for review (if distributing publicly)

docs.title: 3.1 Get a Mozilla Add-on Developer Account
docs.text:
1. Go to https://addons.mozilla.org/developers/
  2. Sign in with Firefox Account (or create one)
  3. Agree to the Developer Agreement

docs.title: 3.2 Build the Extension
docs.text:
cd extensions/firefox
./build.sh

This creates build/zen-browser-bridge-4.0.0.zip

docs.title: 3.3 Option A: Self-Distribution (Unlisted)
docs.text:
Use this if you want to host the extension yourself (not on the store):

  1. Go to https://addons.mozilla.org/developers/addon/submit/upload-unlisted
  2. Upload build/zen-browser-bridge-4.0.0.zip
  3. Wait for automated validation (usually instant)
  4. Download the signed .xpi file
  5. Distribute the signed .xpi to users

Advantages: - No review process - Fast (usually minutes) - Can distribute via your own website/GitHub

How users install: - Users download the signed .xpi - Drag and drop into Firefox - Extension stays permanently installed

docs.title: 3.4 Option B: Firefox Add-ons Store (Listed)
docs.text:
Use this for public distribution on the official store:

  1. Go to https://addons.mozilla.org/developers/addon/submit/distribution
  2. Choose "On this site" (listed)
  3. Upload build/zen-browser-bridge-4.0.0.zip
  4. Fill out listing information:
  5. Name: Inspekt
  6. Summary: Execute JavaScript in your browser from the command line
  7. Categories: Developer Tools
  8. Support email/website
  9. Submit for review

Review process: - Mozilla reviews the extension (can take days to weeks) - Once approved, it appears on addons.mozilla.org - Users can install with one click

Advantages: - Maximum visibility and trust - One-click installation for users - Automatic updates

docs.title: Method 4: Use web-ext for Development
docs.text: Best for: Active development and testing

docs.title: 4.1 Install web-ext
docs.text:
npm install -g web-ext

Or use npx (no installation needed): 

npx web-ext --version

docs.title: 4.2 Run Extension in Temporary Profile
docs.text:
cd extensions/firefox
web-ext run

This opens a new Firefox window with the extension loaded.

docs.title: 4.3 Run with Your Firefox Profile
docs.text: web-ext run --firefox-profile=/path/to/profile

docs.title: 4.4 Build and Sign
docs.text:
# Build
web-ext build

# Sign (requires API credentials)
web-ext sign --api-key=your-key --api-secret=your-secret

Get API credentials: 1. Go to https://addons.mozilla.org/developers/addon/api/key/ 2. Generate API credentials 3. Use them with web-ext

docs.title: Comparison Table
docs.text: Method Permanent Regular Firefox Setup Complexity Best For Temporary ❌ No ✅ Yes ⭐ Easy Testing, quick use Unsigned (Dev Edition) ✅ Yes ❌ No ⭐⭐ Medium Development Self-Signed (Unlisted) ✅ Yes ✅ Yes ⭐⭐⭐ Medium Self-distribution Store (Listed) ✅ Yes ✅ Yes ⭐⭐⭐⭐ Hard Public distribution web-ext ❌ Temporary ✅ Yes ⭐⭐ Medium Active development

docs.title: For Sharing with Friends/Team

docs.text: Solution: Make sure you're using Firefox Developer Edition/Nightly with signature verification disabled, or use a signed .xpi file.

docs.text: Solution: This is expected behavior. Use Method 2 or 3 for permanent installation.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Customize Inspekt for your specific workflow with comprehensive configuration options. This guide covers everything from basic settings to advanced control mode customization.

docs.title: Configuration File Location
docs.text:
Inspekt uses a JSON configuration file:

config.json

The file is located in the project root directory where you installed Inspekt.

Create Config File

If config.json doesn't exist, create it in the project root: 

cd /path/to/zen-bridge
touch config.json

docs.title: Configuration Structure
docs.text:
The configuration file has two main sections:

  1. ai-language - Language for AI operations (summarize, describe)
  2. control - Keyboard control mode settings

docs.title: Complete Default Configuration
docs.text:
{
  "ai-language": "auto",
  "control": {
    "auto-refocus": "only-spa",
    "focus-outline": "custom",
    "speak-name": false,
    "speak-all": true,
    "announce-role": false,
    "announce-on-page-load": false,
    "navigation-wrap": true,
    "scroll-on-focus": true,
    "click-delay": 0,
    "focus-color": "#0066ff",
    "focus-size": 3,
    "focus-animation": true,
    "focus-glow": true,
    "sound-on-focus": "none",
    "selector-strategy": "id-first",
    "refocus-timeout": 2000,
    "verbose": true,
    "verbose-logging": false
  }
}

docs.title: ai-language
docs.text:
Controls the language used for AI-powered features (inspektsummarize and inspektdescribe).

Type: string Default: "auto" Options: "auto", "en", "nl", "fr", "de", "es", etc.

Auto-detect (Default)Fixed LanguageMultiple Languages 
{
  "ai-language": "auto"
}

Automatically detects the page language and uses it for AI operations.

{
  "ai-language": "en"
}

Always use English for AI operations, regardless of page language.

{
  "ai-language": "nl"
}

Use Dutch for summaries and descriptions.

Supported Languages: Any language code supported by your AI provider (mods).

Requires mods

AI features require mods to be installed. The language setting is passed to the AI model in the prompt.

docs.title: Control Mode Configuration
docs.text: The control section customizes keyboard navigation behavior when using inspektcontrol.

docs.title: auto-refocus
docs.text:
When to automatically refocus the previously focused element after page navigation.

Type: "always" | "only-spa" | "never" Default: "only-spa"

only-spa (Default)alwaysnever 
{
  "control": {
    "auto-refocus": "only-spa"
  }
}

Only refocus on Single Page Applications (SPAs) where the URL changes without a full page reload.

Use case: Modern web apps like Gmail, Twitter, GitHub.

{
  "control": {
    "auto-refocus": "always"
  }
}

Always try to refocus after any page change, including full page reloads.

Use case: Aggressive refocus behavior for maximum continuity.

{
  "control": {
    "auto-refocus": "never"
  }
}

Never automatically refocus. Focus returns to <body> after navigation.

Use case: You prefer manual navigation from the top of each page.

docs.title: refocus-timeout
docs.text:
Maximum time to wait for refocus operation to complete.

Type: number (milliseconds) Default: 2000 Range: 100 - 10000

{
  "control": {
    "refocus-timeout": 2000
  }
}

Increase for slow-loading pages, decrease for faster feedback.

docs.title: focus-outline
docs.text:
Visual style for focused elements.

Type: "custom" | "original" | "none" Default: "custom"

custom (Default)originalnone 
{
  "control": {
    "focus-outline": "custom"
  }
}

Use Inspekt's custom blue outline with glow effect.

{
  "control": {
    "focus-outline": "original"
  }
}

Keep the browser's default focus outline.

{
  "control": {
    "focus-outline": "none"
  }
}

No focus outline (not recommended for accessibility).

docs.title: focus-color
docs.text:
Color of the custom focus outline.

Type: string (CSS color) Default: "#0066ff"

{
  "control": {
    "focus-color": "#ff6600"
  }
}

Examples:

  • "#0066ff" - Blue (default)
  • "#ff0000" - Red
  • "rgb(255, 0, 0)" - Red (RGB)
  • "orange" - Orange (named color)

docs.title: focus-size
docs.text:
Width of the focus outline in pixels.

Type: number (pixels) Default: 3 Range: 1 - 10

{
  "control": {
    "focus-size": 5
  }
}

Larger values create more prominent outlines.

docs.title: focus-animation
docs.text:
Enable animated focus transitions.

Type: boolean Default: true

{
  "control": {
    "focus-animation": true
  }
}

Smooth fade-in effect when focus changes.

docs.title: focus-glow
docs.text:
Enable glow effect around focused elements.

Type: boolean Default: true

{
  "control": {
    "focus-glow": true
  }
}

Adds a soft glow shadow for better visibility.

docs.title: navigation-wrap
docs.text:
Whether navigation wraps from last element to first (and vice versa).

Type: boolean Default: true

{
  "control": {
    "navigation-wrap": true
  }
}

When true, pressing Tab on the last focusable element jumps to the first.

docs.title: scroll-on-focus
docs.text:
Automatically scroll focused elements into view.

Type: boolean Default: true

{
  "control": {
    "scroll-on-focus": true
  }
}

Ensures focused elements are always visible.

docs.title: click-delay
docs.text:
Delay before executing click actions (in milliseconds).

Type: number (milliseconds) Default: 0 Range: 0 - 5000

{
  "control": {
    "click-delay": 100
  }
}

Useful if pages need time to settle before clicks.

docs.title: sound-on-focus
docs.text:
Play a sound when focus changes.

Type: "none" | "beep" | "click" | "subtle" Default: "none"

none (Default)beepclicksubtle 
{
  "control": {
    "sound-on-focus": "none"
  }
}

No sound effects.

{
  "control": {
    "sound-on-focus": "beep"
  }
}

Short beep on focus change.

{
  "control": {
    "sound-on-focus": "click"
  }
}

Click sound on focus change.

{
  "control": {
    "sound-on-focus": "subtle"
  }
}

Subtle tone on focus change.

Browser Support

Sound effects require browser support for the Web Audio API.

docs.title: speak-all
docs.text:
Speak all terminal output via text-to-speech (macOS only).

Type: boolean Default: true

{
  "control": {
    "speak-all": true
  }
}

Uses macOS say command to read terminal messages aloud.

docs.title: speak-name
docs.text:
Speak element name when focused.

Type: boolean Default: false

{
  "control": {
    "speak-name": true
  }
}

Announces accessible name of focused element (from aria-label, text content, etc.).

docs.title: announce-role
docs.text:
Announce element role (button, link, heading, etc.).

Type: boolean Default: false

{
  "control": {
    "announce-role": true
  }
}

Example: "Submit button" instead of just "Submit".

docs.title: announce-on-page-load
docs.text:
Announce page title when a new page loads.

Type: boolean Default: false

{
  "control": {
    "announce-on-page-load": true
  }
}

Helps orient you when navigating between pages.

docs.title: selector-strategy
docs.text:
Strategy for generating element selectors for refocus operations.

Type: "id-first" | "aria-first" | "css-first" Default: "id-first"

id-first (Default)aria-firstcss-first 
{
  "control": {
    "selector-strategy": "id-first"
  }
}

Prefer id attributes, fall back to ARIA, then CSS selectors.

Best for: Most web pages with proper IDs.

{
  "control": {
    "selector-strategy": "aria-first"
  }
}

Prefer ARIA labels, fall back to ID, then CSS.

Best for: Accessibility-focused applications.

{
  "control": {
    "selector-strategy": "css-first"
  }
}

Use CSS selectors based on tag/class/structure.

Best for: Pages with dynamic IDs.

docs.title: verbose
docs.text:
Show detailed terminal announcements during control mode.

Type: boolean Default: true

{
  "control": {
    "verbose": true
  }
}

When true, prints messages like "Focused: Submit button" to the terminal.

docs.title: verbose-logging
docs.text:
Enable verbose logging in the browser console.

Type: boolean Default: false

{
  "control": {
    "verbose-logging": true
  }
}

Useful for debugging control mode behavior. Check browser DevTools console.

docs.title: Minimal Configuration
docs.text:
For users who just want AI in a different language:

{
  "ai-language": "nl"
}

All control settings use defaults.

docs.title: Accessibility-Focused Configuration
docs.text:
For users relying on screen readers and audio feedback:

{
  "ai-language": "en",
  "control": {
    "auto-refocus": "always",
    "speak-all": true,
    "speak-name": true,
    "announce-role": true,
    "announce-on-page-load": true,
    "sound-on-focus": "subtle",
    "verbose": true,
    "selector-strategy": "aria-first"
  }
}

docs.title: Performance-Optimized Configuration
docs.text:
Minimal visual effects for faster performance:

{
  "ai-language": "auto",
  "control": {
    "focus-animation": false,
    "focus-glow": false,
    "scroll-on-focus": false,
    "speak-all": false,
    "verbose": false,
    "verbose-logging": false
  }
}

docs.title: High-Contrast Configuration
docs.text:
Enhanced visibility with bold outlines:

{
  "ai-language": "auto",
  "control": {
    "focus-outline": "custom",
    "focus-color": "#ffff00",
    "focus-size": 5,
    "focus-animation": true,
    "focus-glow": true
  }
}

docs.title: Developer/Debug Configuration
docs.text:
Maximum logging and visibility:

{
  "ai-language": "auto",
  "control": {
    "auto-refocus": "always",
    "verbose": true,
    "verbose-logging": true,
    "refocus-timeout": 5000,
    "focus-color": "#ff00ff",
    "focus-size": 4
  }
}

docs.title: Reload Configuration
docs.text:
Configuration is loaded when:

  1. Server starts - inspektserver start
  2. Control mode starts - inspektcontrol

To apply changes:

Restart Control ModeRestart Server 
# Press 'q' in control mode to quit, then restart
inspektcontrol

inspektserver stop
inspektserver start --daemon

Live Reload

Control mode configuration is sent to the browser when you start inspektcontrol, so you just need to quit and restart control mode to apply changes.

docs.title: Customizing AI Prompts
docs.text: AI prompts are stored in separate files for easy customization:

docs.title: Summary Prompt
docs.text:
Location: prompts/summary.prompt

Edit this file to change how articles are summarized:

Provide a concise, structured summary of the following article.
Focus on the main points and key takeaways.

Article content:
{content}

docs.title: Description Prompt
docs.text:
Location: prompts/describe.prompt

Edit this file to change how pages are described:

Describe this webpage in a way that would be helpful for someone
using a screen reader. Focus on navigation, main content, and structure.

Page structure:
{content}

Variables available: {content}, {url}, {title}, {language}

docs.title: Configuration Hierarchy
docs.text:
Configuration is loaded in the following order (later values override earlier ones):

  1. Default values (hardcoded in zen/domain/models.py)
  2. config.json (project root)
  3. Command-line flags (where applicable)

Example:

# Default verbose=true, but config.json sets verbose=false
# Result: verbose=false

# But if you pass a flag:
inspektcontrol --verbose
# Result: verbose=true (flag overrides config)

No CLI Flags for Config

Currently, Inspekt doesn't support command-line flags for most configuration options. Edit config.json to customize behavior.

docs.title: Configuration Not Loading
docs.text:
Problem: Changes to config.json don't seem to apply.

Solutions:

  1. Check JSON syntax: 

    # Validate JSON
python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('config.json'))"

  2. Check file location: 

    # Ensure config.json is in project root
ls -la config.json

  3. Restart server and control mode: 

    inspektserver stop
inspektserver start --daemon
inspektcontrol

docs.title: Invalid Configuration Value
docs.text:
Problem: Server or control mode fails to start.

Solution: Check for invalid values:

  • auto-refocus: Must be "always", "only-spa", or "never"
  • focus-outline: Must be "custom", "original", or "none"
  • sound-on-focus: Must be "none", "beep", "click", or "subtle"
  • selector-strategy: Must be "id-first", "aria-first", or "css-first"
  • refocus-timeout: Must be number >= 100
  • focus-size: Must be number >= 1

docs.title: Configuration Ignored
docs.text:
Problem: Some settings don't seem to work.

Check:

  1. Feature support: Some features (like TTS) only work on macOS
  2. Browser compatibility: Sound effects require Web Audio API
  3. Spelling: JSON keys are case-sensitive and use hyphens

docs.title: Advanced: Programmatic Configuration
docs.text:
You can load and validate configuration programmatically:

from zen.domain.models import ZenConfig

# Load from file
with open('config.json') as f:
    config_dict = json.load(f)

# Validate with Pydantic
config = ZenConfig(**config_dict)

# Access settings
print(config.ai_language)  # "auto"
print(config.control.auto_refocus)  # "only-spa"
print(config.control.focus_color)  # "#0066ff"

This is useful for building extensions or integrating Inspekt into other tools.

docs.text:

docs.title: Recording and Replay Audio
docs.text: The audio section controls audio feedback during inspekt record and inspekt replay.

docs.title: audio.output
docs.text:
Where to play audio feedback sounds.

Type: "cli" | "browser" | "off" Default: "cli"

cli (Default)browseroff 
{
  "audio": {
    "output": "cli"
  }
}

Play sounds via system audio (macOS afplay, Linux aplay).

Advantages: - Works immediately, no browser interaction needed - Plays asynchronously, doesn't slow down replay - Works over SSH if your terminal supports audio

{
  "audio": {
    "output": "browser"
  }
}

Play sounds via Web Audio API in the browser.

Note: Requires clicking in the browser window first (browser autoplay policy).

Use case: When terminal audio is not available.

{
  "audio": {
    "output": "off"
  }
}

Disable all audio feedback.

Use case: CI/CD environments, quiet operation.

docs.title: audio.volume
docs.text:
Volume level for audio feedback.

Type: number (0.0 to 1.0) Default: 0.5

{
  "audio": {
    "output": "cli",
    "volume": 0.7
  }
}

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text:
Quick reference for all available settings:

Setting Type Default Description ai-language string "auto" Language for AI operations audio.output string "cli" Audio output: cli, browser, or off audio.volume number 0.5 Audio volume (0.0 to 1.0) control.auto-refocus string "only-spa" When to auto-refocus control.focus-outline string "custom" Focus outline style control.speak-name boolean false Speak element name control.speak-all boolean true Speak all terminal output control.announce-role boolean false Announce element role control.announce-on-page-load boolean false Announce page title on load control.navigation-wrap boolean true Wrap navigation at end control.scroll-on-focus boolean true Scroll to focused element control.click-delay number 0 Delay before clicks (ms) control.focus-color string "#0066ff" Focus outline color control.focus-size number 3 Focus outline width (px) control.focus-animation boolean true Animate focus transitions control.focus-glow boolean true Add glow effect control.sound-on-focus string "none" Sound on focus change control.selector-strategy string "id-first" Element selector strategy control.refocus-timeout number 2000 Refocus timeout (ms) control.verbose boolean true Terminal announcements control.verbose-logging boolean false Browser console logging

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: This comprehensive guide will walk you through installing Inspekt on your system, from installing Python dependencies to setting up the browser userscript and verifying everything works correctly.

docs.title: Installation Flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Install CLI] --> B[Install Userscript]
    B --> C[Start Server]
    C --> D[Test Connection]
    D --> E[Ready!]

    style A fill:#e1f5ff
    style B fill:#fff4e1
    style C fill:#ffe1f5
    style D fill:#fff9e6
    style E fill:#e1ffe1

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Before you begin, ensure you have the following:

  • Python 3.11 or higher - Check your version with python --version or python3 --version
  • pip - Python package manager (usually included with Python)
  • A modern browser - Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, or any Chromium-based browser
  • A userscript manager extension - We'll install this in the browser setup step

Python Version Check

Run python3 --version to check your Python version. If you have Python 3.10 or lower, you'll need to upgrade to Python 3.11 or higher.

macOSUbuntu/DebianWindows 
# Using Homebrew
brew install python@3.11

sudo apt update
sudo apt install python3.11 python3.11-pip

Download from python.org and install Python 3.11+

docs.title: Step 1: Install the CLI Tool
docs.text:
You can install Inspekt from source (recommended for development) or via pip (when available).

From Source (Recommended)Install Dependencies ManuallyFor Development

Clone the repository and install in development mode:

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/roelvangils/inspekt.git
cd inspekt

# Install in development mode
pip install -e .

This installs the zen command and all dependencies. The -e flag means "editable" - changes to the source code will be reflected immediately.

If you prefer to manage dependencies yourself:

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/roelvangils/inspekt.git
cd inspekt

# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

If you plan to contribute or run tests:

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/roelvangils/inspekt.git
cd inspekt

# Install with dev dependencies
pip install -e ".[dev]"

This includes testing tools (pytest, playwright), linters (ruff), and type checkers (mypy).

docs.title: Verify the Installation
docs.text:
After installation, verify the zen command is available:

inspekt--version

You should see output like:

Inspekt v2.0.0

Run the help command to see available commands:

inspekt--help

Installation Complete

The CLI tool is now installed! Next, we'll set up the browser connection.

docs.title: Step 2: Install the Browser Component
docs.text:
The browser needs a component to receive commands from the CLI and establish a WebSocket connection to the server.

Choose one installation method:

  • Extension (Recommended) - Works on ALL websites including GitHub, Gmail, banking sites. Bypasses CSP restrictions.
  • Userscript (Quick Setup) - One-click installation, but may be blocked by CSP on some sites.

docs.title: Extension Installation
docs.text: The Firefox extension provides full compatibility with all websites, including those with strict Content Security Policy (CSP) like GitHub, Gmail, and banking sites.

docs.title: 2.1a Install Firefox Extension
docs.text:
1. Download the extension files from the repository: 

    cd /path/to/inspekt
cd extensions/firefox

  2. Open Firefox and navigate to: 

    about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox

  3. Load the extension:

  4. Click "Load Temporary Add-on..."

  5. Select the manifest.json file from extensions/firefox/

  6. Verify installation:

  7. Look for the ⚡ icon in your toolbar
  8. Click it to see the status panel

Extension Installed

The extension will now work on all websites! Continue to Step 3: Start the Bridge Server.

Why Use the Extension?

The extension bypasses Content Security Policy (CSP) restrictions that block the userscript on important sites:

  • ✅ Works on GitHub, Gmail, banking sites
  • ✅ Built-in settings panel with connection status
  • ✅ No CSP limitations

Read more about extensions →

docs.title: Userscript Installation
docs.text: The userscript is quick to install but may be blocked by CSP on some websites. If you encounter issues on GitHub, Gmail, or banking sites, use the extension instead.

docs.title: 2.1b Install a Userscript Manager
docs.text:
First, install a userscript manager extension in your browser:

Violentmonkey (Recommended)TampermonkeyGreasemonkey (Firefox only)

Best compatibility and open source.

  • Chrome/Edge
  • Firefox
  • Safari

Popular alternative with many features.

  • Chrome/Edge
  • Firefox
  • Safari

Classic Firefox userscript manager.

  • Firefox

Browser Compatibility

Inspekt works with any browser that supports userscript managers and WebSockets. This includes all modern browsers.

CSP Limitations

The userscript may be blocked by Content Security Policy on sites like:

  • GitHub, GitLab
  • Gmail, Outlook
  • Banking and government sites

If you encounter CSP issues, use the Firefox extension instead for full compatibility.

Read CSP troubleshooting guide →

docs.title: 2.2b Get the Userscript Code
docs.text:
Display the userscript code using the CLI:

inspektuserscript

This will output the complete userscript code to your terminal. The userscript is located at /Users/roelvangils/zen_bridge/userscript_ws.js in the repository.

docs.title: 2.3b Create the Userscript
docs.text:
Now create a new userscript in your userscript manager:

  1. Click the userscript manager icon in your browser toolbar
  2. Create a new script (usually a "+" or "New Script" button)
  3. Delete any default content in the editor
  4. Paste the userscript code from the inspektuserscript command
  5. Save the script (usually Ctrl+S or Cmd+S)

The userscript will automatically enable itself.

Quick Copy

To copy the userscript to your clipboard (macOS): 

inspektuserscript | pbcopy

Or save it to a file: 

inspektuserscript > my-userscript.js

docs.title: 2.4b Verify Userscript is Active
docs.text:
To verify the userscript is running:

  1. Open your browser's Developer Console (F12 or Cmd+Option+I)
  2. Look for a message like: "Inspekt userscript loaded"
  3. Check that the userscript manager shows the script as enabled

Userscript Scope

By default, the userscript runs on all pages (@match *://*/*). If you want to restrict it to specific domains, edit the @match line in the userscript.

docs.title: Step 3: Start the Bridge Server
docs.text: The bridge server acts as a middleman between the CLI and browser, managing WebSocket connections and HTTP endpoints.

docs.title: 3.1 Start the Server
docs.text:
You can start the server in foreground or background mode:

Background Mode (Daemon)Foreground Mode

Recommended for normal use:

inspektserver start --daemon

The server runs in the background. You can close your terminal and it will keep running.

Check server status: 

inspektserver status

Stop the server: 

inspektserver stop

Useful for debugging:

inspektserver start

The server runs in the foreground with live log output. Press Ctrl+C to stop.

Example output: 

Starting Inspekt WebSocket server...
HTTP API server: http://127.0.0.1:8765
WebSocket server: ws://127.0.0.1:8766
Server is ready! Waiting for browser connections...

docs.title: 3.2 Server Ports
docs.text:
The server uses two ports:

  • HTTP API: http://127.0.0.1:8765 - CLI communicates with this
  • WebSocket: ws://127.0.0.1:8766 - Browser connects to this

Port Configuration

The ports are currently hardcoded. If you need to change them, you'll need to modify the server configuration and userscript.

docs.title: 3.3 Verify Server is Running
docs.text:
Check the server status:

inspektserver status

Expected output when running:

✓ Server is running
  PID: 12345
  HTTP API: http://127.0.0.1:8765
  WebSocket: ws://127.0.0.1:8766
  Connected browsers: 0
  Uptime: 2 minutes

docs.title: Step 4: Verify the Complete Setup
docs.text: Now let's verify that everything is working together:

docs.title: 4.1 Open a Browser Tab
docs.text:
1. Open your browser (with the userscript manager and userscript installed)
  2. Navigate to any website, for example: https://example.com
  3. Keep the tab active (the userscript only works in active tabs)

docs.title: 4.2 Check Browser Connection
docs.text:
In the browser's Developer Console (F12), you should see:

Inspekt userscript loaded
Connected to Inspekt WebSocket server

docs.title: 4.3 Execute a Test Command
docs.text:
From your terminal, run a simple command:

inspekteval "document.title"

Expected output:

Example Domain

If you see the page title, congratulations! Everything is working correctly.

Connection Successful!

Your terminal is now connected to your browser. You can execute JavaScript directly in the active tab!

docs.title: 4.4 Try More Commands
docs.text:
# Get page information
inspektinfo

# Get the current URL
inspekteval "location.href"

# Count links on the page
inspekteval "document.querySelectorAll('a').length"

# Start interactive REPL
inspektrepl

Setup Complete!

You've successfully installed Inspekt! Check out the Quick Start Guide for a hands-on tutorial.

docs.title: "zen: command not found"
docs.text:
Problem: The zen command is not in your PATH.

Solutions:

Check InstallationUpdate PATHUse python -m 
# Verify installation
pip show inspekt

# Reinstall if needed
pip install -e .

# Find where pip installs scripts
python3 -m site --user-base

# Add to PATH (add to ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc)
export PATH="$PATH:$(python3 -m site --user-base)/bin"

# Run as a module instead
python3 -m zen.cli --help

docs.title: "Bridge server is not running"
docs.text:
Problem: The CLI cannot connect to the server.

Solutions:

  1. Start the server: 

    inspektserver start --daemon

  2. Check if server is running: 

    inspektserver status

  3. Restart the server: 

    inspektserver stop
inspektserver start --daemon

  4. Check for port conflicts: 

    # Check if ports 8765 or 8766 are in use
lsof -i :8765
lsof -i :8766

docs.title: "No response from browser"
docs.text:
Problem: The browser is not connected to the WebSocket server.

Solutions:

  1. Verify userscript is installed and enabled
  2. Check userscript manager icon

  3. Ensure script is enabled

  4. Check browser console for errors

  5. Open DevTools (F12)
  6. Look for WebSocket connection errors

  7. Ensure you see "Connected to Inspekt WebSocket server"

  8. Ensure tab is active

  9. The userscript only works in the currently active browser tab

  10. Switch to the tab and try again

  11. Restart everything: 

    # Stop server
inspektserver stop

# Restart browser (to reload userscript)

# Start server
inspektserver start --daemon

  12. Check WebSocket connection manually

  13. In browser console, run: 
    ws = new WebSocket('ws://127.0.0.1:8766')
ws.onopen = () => console.log('Connected!')

docs.title: Command Timeout
docs.text:
Problem: Commands hang or timeout.

Solutions:

  1. Increase timeout: 

    inspekteval "slow_operation()" --timeout 30

  2. Check if tab is active:

  3. Inactive tabs may throttle JavaScript execution

  4. Switch to the tab and try again

  5. Check for JavaScript errors:

  6. Open browser console
  7. Look for errors when command executes

docs.title: WebSocket Connection Refused
docs.text:
Problem: Browser cannot connect to WebSocket server.

Solutions:

  1. Verify server is running: 

    inspektserver status

  2. Check firewall settings:

  3. Ensure localhost connections are allowed

  4. Port 8766 must be accessible

  5. Try a different port (requires code modification):

  6. Edit server configuration
  7. Update userscript to match

docs.title: Python Version Issues
docs.text:
Problem: Inspekt requires Python 3.11+, but you have an older version.

Solution: Upgrade Python:

macOS (Homebrew)Ubuntu/DebianWindows 
brew install python@3.11
# Update PATH in ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc
export PATH="/usr/local/opt/python@3.11/bin:$PATH"

sudo apt update
sudo apt install python3.11 python3.11-pip
# Use python3.11 explicitly
python3.11 -m pip install -e .

Download and install from python.org

docs.title: Uninstallation
docs.text: To uninstall Inspekt:

docs.title: 1. Stop the Server
docs.text: inspektserver stop

docs.title: 2. Uninstall the Package
docs.text:
# If installed with pip
pip uninstall inspekt

# If installed from source, just delete the directory
rm -rf ~/inspekt

docs.title: 3. Remove Browser Userscript
docs.text:
1. Click userscript manager icon
  2. Find "Inspekt" script
  3. Delete or disable the script

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
Now that you have Inspekt installed, continue with:

  • Quick Start Guide - 5-minute hands-on tutorial
  • Configuration - Customize your setup
  • User Guide - Learn all commands and features

docs.text:

  • Architecture Guide - How Inspekt works internally

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Get up and running with Inspekt in just 5 minutes! This hands-on tutorial will walk you through the basics and show you the power of browser automation from the command line.

Prerequisites

Make sure you've completed the Installation guide before starting this tutorial.

docs.title: Quick Start Workflow
docs.text:
Here's what we'll cover in this tutorial:

graph LR
    A[Execute JavaScript] --> B[Use REPL]
    B --> C[Extract Data]
    C --> D[Automate Tasks]
    D --> E[Advanced Features]

    style A fill:#e1f5ff
    style B fill:#fff4e1
    style C fill:#ffe1f5
    style D fill:#fff9e6
    style E fill:#e1ffe1

docs.title: Step 1: Navigate to a Test Page
docs.text: Open your browser and navigate to https://example.com. Keep this tab active.

docs.title: Step 2: Execute JavaScript
docs.text:
Run your first command to get the page title:

inspekteval "document.title"

Expected output:

Example Domain

Congratulations! You just executed JavaScript in your browser from the terminal.

docs.title: Step 3: Try More Expressions
docs.text:
# Get the current URL
inspekteval "location.href"
# => https://example.com/

# Count paragraphs on the page
inspekteval "document.querySelectorAll('p').length"
# => 2

# Get all link URLs
inspekteval "Array.from(document.links).map(a => a.href)"
# => ["https://www.iana.org/domains/example"]

Quick Tip

The inspekteval command evaluates JavaScript expressions. For more complex code, use inspektexec with a file.

docs.title: Interactive REPL Session
docs.text:
The REPL (Read-Eval-Print Loop) lets you experiment with JavaScript interactively:

inspektrepl

Try these commands in the REPL:

// Get the page title
zen> document.title
"Example Domain"

// Query the DOM
zen> document.querySelectorAll('h1')[0].textContent
"Example Domain"

// Create an array of links
zen> Array.from(document.links).map(a => ({text: a.textContent, href: a.href}))
[{text: "More information...", href: "https://www.iana.org/domains/example"}]

// Exit the REPL
zen> exit
Goodbye!

REPL Power

The REPL is perfect for exploring APIs, debugging, and prototyping JavaScript code before adding it to scripts.

docs.title: Extract Page Information
docs.text:
Use the info command to get comprehensive page details:

inspektinfo

Example output:

URL:      https://example.com
Title:    Example Domain
Domain:   example.com
Protocol: https:
State:    complete
Size:     1280x720

For extended information including language, meta tags, and cookies:

inspektinfo --extended

docs.title: Working with Links
docs.text: Navigate to a page with more links (like a news site or blog), then:

docs.title: List All Links
docs.text:
inspektlinks

Example output:

→ Home Page
  https://example.com/

→ About Us
  https://example.com/about

↗ External Resource
  https://other-site.com/page

Total: 15 links (12 internal, 3 external)

docs.title: Extract External Links Only
docs.text:
inspektlinks --only-external --only-urls

This outputs just the URLs, one per line - perfect for piping to other tools.

docs.title: Save Links to a File
docs.text: inspektlinks --only-urls > all-links.txt

docs.title: Get Enriched Link Metadata
docs.text:
inspektlinks --only-external --enrich-external

This fetches additional metadata like MIME types, file sizes, and HTTP status codes.

docs.title: Click an Element
docs.text:
# Click by CSS selector
inspektclick "button#submit"

# Double-click
inspektdouble-click "div.editable"

# Right-click (context menu)
inspektright-click "a.download"

docs.title: Highlight Elements
docs.text:
Useful for visual debugging:

# Highlight all headings
inspekthighlight "h1, h2, h3"

# Custom color
inspekthighlight "a" --color blue

# Clear highlights
inspekthighlight --clear

docs.title: Wait for Elements
docs.text:
Perfect for automation:

# Wait for element to exist (default: 30s timeout)
inspektwait "button#submit"

# Wait for element to be visible
inspektwait ".modal-dialog" --visible

# Wait for element to be hidden
inspektwait ".loading-spinner" --hidden

# Wait for text content
inspektwait "div.result" --text "Success"

# Custom timeout (10 seconds)
inspektwait "div.notification" --timeout 10

docs.title: View Heading Hierarchy
docs.text:
inspektoutline

Example output:

H1 Getting Started
   H2 Installation
      H3 Prerequisites
      H3 Setup
   H2 Configuration
      H3 Basic Settings
      H3 Advanced Options
         H4 Environment Variables

Total: 7 headings

This is great for:

  • Accessibility audits
  • SEO analysis
  • Understanding page structure

docs.title: Extract Table Data
docs.text: inspektexec zen/scripts/extract_table.js --format json > data.json

docs.title: Extract All Images
docs.text: inspektexec zen/scripts/extract_images.js --format json

docs.title: Get SEO Metadata
docs.text: inspektexec zen/scripts/extract_metadata.js --format json

docs.title: Custom Extraction
docs.text:
Extract product prices (example):

inspekteval "
  Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.product')).map(p => ({
    name: p.querySelector('.name').textContent,
    price: p.querySelector('.price').textContent
  }))
" --format json

Format Options

Use --format json for structured output, --format raw for plain text, or --format default for human-readable output.

docs.title: AI-Powered Features
docs.text:
Requires mods

AI features require mods to be installed.

docs.title: Summarize an Article
docs.text:
Navigate to a news article or blog post, then:

inspektsummarize

This extracts the article content using Mozilla Readability and generates a concise summary.

docs.title: Describe a Page for Screen Readers
docs.text:
inspektdescribe

Example output:

This webpage is in English. At the top you can navigate to Home, About,
Services, and Contact. The main part contains an article about browser
automation with three headings. The footer contains links to Privacy
Policy and Terms of Service.

Perfect for understanding page structure before diving into automation.

docs.title: Form Automation Example
docs.text:
Let's automate filling out a login form:

# Fill email field
inspekteval "document.querySelector('#email').value = 'user@example.com'"

# Fill password field
inspekteval "document.querySelector('#password').value = 'mypassword'"

# Click submit button
inspektclick "button[type=submit]"

# Wait for success message
inspektwait ".success-message" --visible

# Verify we're logged in
inspekteval "document.querySelector('.user-name').textContent"

Security Note

Be careful with passwords in command history! See the Security Guide for best practices.

docs.title: Navigation Commands
docs.text:
# Navigate to a URL
inspektopen https://example.com

# Navigate and wait for page load
inspektopen https://example.com --wait

# Go back in history
inspektback

# Go forward in history
inspektforward

# Reload the page
inspektreload

# Hard reload (bypass cache)
inspektreload --hard

docs.title: Get Selected Text
docs.text:
Select some text in the browser, then:

# Get selected text with metadata
inspektselected

# Raw text only
inspektselected --raw

# Copy to clipboard (macOS)
inspektselected --raw | pbcopy

docs.title: Send Text to Browser
docs.text:
Type text character by character into focused field:

# Type into currently focused field
inspektsend "Hello World"

# Type into specific field
inspektsend "test@example.com" --selector "input[type=email]"

docs.title: Keyboard Control Mode
docs.text:
Navigate pages entirely with your keyboard:

inspektcontrol

Controls:

  • Tab / Shift+Tab - Navigate forward/backward
  • Up Down Left Right - Move focus directionally
  • Enter / Space - Activate focused element
  • Esc - Return to body
  • Q - Quit control mode

Features:

  • Auto-refocus after page navigation
  • Visual feedback (blue outlines)
  • Real-time terminal announcements
  • Optional text-to-speech (macOS)

Control Mode Configuration

Customize control mode behavior in config.json. See the Configuration Guide.

docs.title: Watch Browser Events
docs.text:
Monitor keyboard input in real-time:

inspektwatch input

Focus any text field in the browser and start typing. The terminal will show each keystroke:

Watching keyboard input... (Press Ctrl+C to stop)
H e l l o [SPACE] W o r l d [ENTER]

Press Ctrl+C to stop watching.

docs.title: Execute JavaScript from Files
docs.text:
Create a file extract-titles.js:

// Extract all headings from the page
const headings = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6'))
  .map(h => ({
    level: h.tagName,
    text: h.textContent.trim(),
    id: h.id
  }));

headings;  // Return value

Execute it:

inspektexec extract-titles.js --format json

Or use the shorthand:

inspektexec extract-titles.js --format json
# Same as:
inspekteval --file extract-titles.js --format json

docs.title: Working with Output Formats
docs.text:
Inspekt supports multiple output formats:

Default (Human-Readable)JSONRaw 
inspekteval "({title: document.title, url: location.href})"

Output: 

{
  title: "Example Domain",
  url: "https://example.com/"
}


inspekteval "({title: document.title, url: location.href})" --format json

Output: 

{
  "title": "Example Domain",
  "url": "https://example.com/"
}


inspekteval "document.title" --format raw

Output: 

Example Domain

No extra formatting - perfect for piping to other commands.

docs.title: Combining with Shell Commands
docs.text:
Inspekt plays nicely with standard Unix tools:

# Count external links
inspektlinks --only-external --only-urls | wc -l

# Find all PDF links
inspektlinks --only-urls | grep "\.pdf$"

# Get unique domains from external links
inspektlinks --only-external --only-urls | sed 's|https\?://\([^/]*\).*|\1|' | sort | uniq

# Export data and process with jq
inspekteval "Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a')).map(a => ({text: a.textContent, href: a.href}))" --format json | jq '.[0:5]'

docs.title: Check if Element Exists
docs.text:
inspekteval "document.querySelector('#element-id') !== null"
# => true or false

docs.title: Get Computed Style
docs.text:
inspekteval "getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('h1')).color"
# => rgb(0, 0, 0)

docs.title: Scroll to Bottom
docs.text: inspekteval "window.scrollTo(0, document.body.scrollHeight)"

docs.title: Take Screenshot of Element
docs.text:
# Screenshot by selector
inspektscreenshot --selector "h1" --output screenshot.png

# Screenshot inspected element (set in DevTools)
inspektscreenshot --selector "$0" --output element.png

docs.title: Monitor for Changes
docs.text:
# Check element count every 5 seconds
while true; do
  inspekteval "document.querySelectorAll('.notification').length" --format raw
  sleep 5
done

docs.title: Extract and Download Files
docs.text:
# Interactive file finder
inspektdownload

# List all downloadable files
inspektdownload --list

# Custom output directory
inspektdownload --output ~/Downloads

docs.title: Command Hangs or Times Out
docs.text:
# Increase timeout (in seconds)
inspekteval "slowOperation()" --timeout 30

docs.title: "No response from browser"
docs.text:
1. Ensure browser tab is active (not in background)
  2. Check browser console for errors (F12)
  3. Verify WebSocket connection in console: 
    // Should see "Connected to Inspekt WebSocket server"

docs.title: Check Server Status

inspektserver status

If server isn't running:

inspektserver start --daemon

docs.title: Practice Challenges
docs.text:
Try these exercises to build your skills:

Challenge 1: Link Analysis

Navigate to your favorite news site and:

  1. Count total links on the homepage
  2. Extract all external links
  3. Find all links containing "privacy" or "terms"
  4. Save results to a file
Solution 
# 1. Count total links
inspekteval "document.querySelectorAll('a').length"

# 2. Extract external links
inspektlinks --only-external --only-urls > external.txt

# 3. Find privacy/terms links
inspektlinks --only-urls | grep -E "(privacy|terms)"

# 4. Already saved in step 2!

Challenge 2: Form Automation

Find a demo contact form online and:

  1. Fill all fields programmatically
  2. Submit the form
  3. Wait for success message
  4. Extract the success message text
Solution 
# 1. Fill fields
inspekteval "document.querySelector('#name').value = 'John Doe'"
inspekteval "document.querySelector('#email').value = 'john@example.com'"
inspekteval "document.querySelector('#message').value = 'Hello!'"

# 2. Submit
inspektclick "button[type=submit]"

# 3. Wait for success
inspektwait ".success-message" --visible

# 4. Extract message
inspekteval "document.querySelector('.success-message').textContent"

Challenge 3: Data Extraction

Navigate to a Wikipedia article and:

  1. Get the article title
  2. Count all sections (h2 headings)
  3. Extract all image URLs
  4. Create JSON with all the data
Solution 
# 1. Get title
inspekteval "document.querySelector('h1').textContent"

# 2. Count sections
inspekteval "document.querySelectorAll('h2').length"

# 3. Extract images
inspekteval "Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('img')).map(img => img.src)"

# 4. Create JSON
inspekteval "{
  title: document.querySelector('h1').textContent,
  sections: document.querySelectorAll('h2').length,
  images: Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('img')).map(img => img.src)
}" --format json > wikipedia.json

docs.text:
Task Command Execute JavaScript inspekteval "code" Interactive REPL inspektrepl Page info inspektinfo Extract links inspektlinks Click element inspektclick "selector" Wait for element inspektwait "selector" --visible Highlight elements inspekthighlight "selector" Page outline inspektoutline AI summary inspektsummarize Page description inspektdescribe Keyboard control inspektcontrol Watch events inspektwatch input Server status inspektserver status Get help inspekt--help

Happy automating! If you run into any issues, check the Troubleshooting section or open an issue on GitHub.

docs.title: Updating Inspekt
docs.text: Keep Inspekt up to date to get the latest features, bug fixes, and improvements.

docs.title: Updating the CLI
docs.text: The Inspekt CLI is installed via pip and can be updated with a single command.

docs.title: Check Current Version
docs.text: inspekt--version

docs.title: Update to Latest Version
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade zen-bridge

Or with pipx:

pipx upgrade zen-bridge

docs.title: Verify Update
docs.text:
inspekt--version
# Should show the new version

inspektserver restart
# Restart the server to use the new version

docs.title: Updating the Userscript
docs.text: The userscript runs in your browser and needs to be updated separately from the CLI.

docs.title: Automatic Updates (Recommended)
docs.text:
Since version 3.5, the userscript supports automatic updates:

  1. Tampermonkey/Violentmonkey will check for updates periodically (usually daily)
  2. You'll be prompted when an update is available
  3. Click "Update" to install the new version

To check manually:

  1. Open Tampermonkey/Violentmonkey dashboard
  2. Find "Inspekt (WebSocket)"
  3. Click the "Check for updates" button
  4. Install if an update is available

docs.title: Manual Update
docs.text:
If you have version 3.4 or earlier (without auto-update):

  1. Open Tampermonkey/Violentmonkey dashboard
  2. Delete the old "Inspekt" script
  3. Visit the raw userscript file: 
    https://raw.githubusercontent.com/roelvangils/zen-bridge/main/userscript_ws.js
  4. Tampermonkey/Violentmonkey will prompt to install the new version
  5. Click "Install"
  6. Reload any open tabs to activate the new version

docs.title: Verify Userscript Version
docs.text:
Open the browser console (F12) and check:

window.__ZEN_BRIDGE_VERSION__
// Should show "3.5" or higher

Or look for the version in the console on page load:

[Inspekt] Connected via WebSocket

docs.title: Version 3.5 (Latest)
docs.text:
New Features: - ✅ CSP (Content Security Policy) detection - ✅ User-friendly warnings when CSP blocks Zen - ✅ Automatic update support via @updateURL - ✅ Better error handling for connection failures

Changes: - Prevents unnecessary reconnection attempts on CSP-blocked sites - Exposes __ZEN_BRIDGE_CSP_BLOCKED__ flag for CLI integration

Documentation: - New troubleshooting guide for CSP issues - Comprehensive explanation of CSP limitations

docs.title: Version 3.4
docs.text: Features: - WebSocket-based communication - DevTools integration with zenStore($0) - Keepalive ping/pong - Auto-reconnection on disconnect - Visibility-based connection management

docs.title: Version 3.x → 4.x (If/When Released)
docs.text: Future major versions may include breaking changes. Check the changelog before updating.

docs.title: Version 2.x → 3.x (Historical)
docs.text:
• Switched from HTTP polling to WebSocket
  • Changed server ports (8765 HTTP API, 8766 WebSocket)
  • Improved reconnection logic

docs.title: CLI Update Issues
docs.text:
Issue: "Command not found" after update

# If using pip
which zen
# Should show path to zen

# If it's missing, reinstall
pip install --force-reinstall zen-bridge

# If using pipx
pipx reinstall zen-bridge

Issue: Old version still showing

# Clear pip cache
pip cache purge

# Reinstall
pip install --upgrade --force-reinstall --no-cache-dir zen-bridge

# Verify
inspekt--version

docs.title: Userscript Update Issues
docs.text:
Issue: Auto-update not working

You may have version 3.4 or earlier without auto-update support. Use the manual update method above.

Issue: Two versions installed

  1. Open Tampermonkey/Violentmonkey dashboard
  2. Look for duplicate "Inspekt" entries
  3. Delete the older version (check version number in script header)
  4. Keep only the latest version

Issue: "Script already installed" error

  1. Delete the existing script first
  2. Then install the new version
  3. Reload browser tabs

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
Check the GitHub Releases page for new versions:

# Check PyPI for latest version
pip index versions zen-bridge

# Compare with your version
inspekt--version

docs.title: Userscript
docs.text:
The userscript version is in the file header:

// @version      3.5

Check the latest version on GitHub.

docs.title: Stay Informed
docs.text:
• Watch the repository on GitHub for release notifications
  • Star the repo to follow development
  • Check the changelog regularly: CHANGELOG.md

docs.title: Automatic Checks
docs.text:
The CLI doesn't currently check for updates automatically. This may be added in a future version.

The userscript (v3.5+) automatically checks for updates via Tampermonkey/Violentmonkey.

docs.title: Downgrading
docs.text: If you need to downgrade due to issues:

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
# Downgrade to specific version
pip install zen-bridge==2.0.0

# Or use pipx
pipx install zen-bridge==2.0.0 --force

docs.title: Userscript
docs.text:
1. Visit the commit history
  2. Find the version you want
  3. Click "View file" on that commit
  4. Click "Raw" to get the direct URL
  5. Install from that URL

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Always update both CLI and userscript together for compatibility
  2. Restart the server after CLI updates: inspektserver restart
  3. Reload browser tabs after userscript updates
  4. Check the changelog before updating for breaking changes
  5. Test after updates to ensure everything works

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text:
If you encounter issues during updates:

  1. Check the Troubleshooting Guide
  2. Visit GitHub Issues
  3. Include your version numbers when reporting problems: 
    inspekt--version
# And userscript version from console

docs.title: Accessibility Testing
docs.text: Learn how to test web accessibility using Inspekt's integrated axe-core testing capabilities. Ensure your websites are accessible to all users, comply with WCAG standards, and catch accessibility issues before they reach production.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Inspekt provides professional accessibility testing through the inspekt axe command, powered by the industry-standard axe-core library from Deque Systems - the same engine that powers Chrome DevTools Lighthouse accessibility audits.

docs.title: Why Accessibility Matters
docs.text:
Legal compliance: - ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act) - Section 508 (US Federal) - EN 301 549 (European Union) - AODA (Ontario, Canada) - Many countries require WCAG 2.0 or 2.1 Level AA

Business benefits: - 15% of global population has some form of disability - Better SEO (accessible sites rank higher) - Improved usability for everyone - Reduced legal risk - Enhanced brand reputation

Technical benefits: - Better semantic HTML structure - Improved keyboard navigation - Clearer content hierarchy - More maintainable code

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Navigate to any page
inspekt open https://example.com

# Run accessibility audit
inspekt axe

# View results

Example output: 

┌─────────────────┬──────────┬───────┬──────────────────────────┐
│ Rule            │ Impact   │ Count │ Description              │
├─────────────────┼──────────┼───────┼──────────────────────────┤
│ color-contrast  │ serious  │ 12    │ Ensure sufficient cont...│
│ image-alt       │ critical │ 3     │ Images must have alt...  │
│ label           │ serious  │ 5     │ Form elements must...    │
└─────────────────┴──────────┴───────┴──────────────────────────┘

Summary: 3 violations (1 critical, 2 serious)
Passes: 45

That's it! You now have a comprehensive accessibility audit of your page.

docs.title: Test Authenticated Content
docs.text:
Unlike browser extensions or standalone tools, Inspekt tests your current browser state:

# You log in manually, navigate to dashboard
inspekt open https://app.example.com
# (Log in through browser UI)

# Audit your actual authenticated session
inspekt axe --level 21aa

# Continue to other logged-in pages
inspekt axe

Test areas other tools can't reach: - User dashboards - Account settings - Admin panels - Private content - Checkout flows - Form validation states

docs.title: Test Dynamic States
docs.text:
Test accessibility at any point in your user journey:

# Test search results after filtering
inspekt open https://store.example.com
# Apply filters in browser (price range, category, etc.)
inspekt axe

# Test modal dialogs
# Click to open modal
inspekt axe  # Tests modal in open state

# Test form error states
# Submit form with validation errors
inspekt axe  # Tests error messages, ARIA live regions

docs.title: Continuous Testing Workflow
docs.text:
# 1. Navigate to feature
inspekt open http://localhost:3000/new-feature

# 2. Test
inspekt axe --level 21aa

# 3. Fix issues in code

# 4. Reload
inspekt reload

# 5. Re-test
inspekt axe --level 21aa

# Repeat until clean

Fast iteration - No browser restart, no re-authentication, no navigation replay.

docs.title: Understanding WCAG Levels
docs.text: WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines) has three conformance levels:

docs.title: Level A (Minimum)
docs.text:
Basic web accessibility - most critical issues: - All images have alt text - Videos have captions - Forms have labels - Headings are in logical order - Keyboard accessible

Test with: 

inspekt axe --level 2a

docs.title: Level AA (Standard) ⭐ Recommended
docs.text:
Standard for most legal requirements: - Everything in Level A - Color contrast meets 4.5:1 ratio - Visible focus indicators - Multiple ways to find pages - Consistent navigation - Error suggestions

Test with: 

inspekt axe --level 2aa      # WCAG 2.0 AA
inspekt axe --level 21aa     # WCAG 2.1 AA (recommended)
inspekt axe --level 22aa     # WCAG 2.2 AA (latest)

Most organizations target WCAG 2.1 Level AA.

docs.title: Level AAA (Enhanced)
docs.text:
Highest level - exceeds legal requirements: - Everything in Level AA - Enhanced color contrast (7:1 ratio) - Sign language interpretation - Extended audio descriptions - Very strict requirements

Test with: 

inspekt axe --level 2aaa

Note: Level AAA is rarely required and very difficult to achieve. Most organizations aim for Level AA.

docs.title: 1. Color Contrast
docs.text:
The problem: Text doesn't have enough contrast against background.

Why it matters: Users with low vision or color blindness can't read content.

WCAG requirement: - Normal text: 4.5:1 contrast ratio (AA), 7:1 (AAA) - Large text (18pt+): 3:1 contrast ratio (AA), 4.5:1 (AAA)

How to fix: 

/* Bad - insufficient contrast */
.text {
  color: #999999;              /* Light gray */
  background-color: #FFFFFF;    /* White */
  /* Contrast: 2.8:1 ❌ */
}

/* Good - sufficient contrast */
.text {
  color: #595959;              /* Darker gray */
  background-color: #FFFFFF;    /* White */
  /* Contrast: 7:1 ✓ */
}

Testing: 

inspekt axe --level 21aa
# Look for "color-contrast" violations

docs.title: 2. Missing Alt Text
docs.text:
The problem: Images lack alternative text.

Why it matters: Screen readers can't describe images to blind users.

How to fix: 

<!-- Bad -->
<img src="product.jpg">

<!-- Good - descriptive alt text -->
<img src="product.jpg" alt="Blue wireless headphones with noise cancellation">

<!-- Good - decorative image -->
<img src="decoration.svg" alt="" role="presentation">

Rules: - Informative images: Describe what the image shows - Functional images: Describe what happens when clicked - Decorative images: Use empty alt (alt="") - Complex images: Provide long description nearby

Testing: 

inspekt axe --level 21aa
# Look for "image-alt" violations

docs.title: 3. Form Labels
docs.text:
The problem: Input fields don't have associated labels.

Why it matters: Screen reader users don't know what to enter.

How to fix: 

<!-- Bad - no label -->
<input type="text" name="email">

<!-- Good - explicit label -->
<label for="email">Email Address</label>
<input type="text" id="email" name="email">

<!-- Good - implicit label -->
<label>
  Email Address
  <input type="text" name="email">
</label>

<!-- Good - ARIA label (use sparingly) -->
<input type="text" name="email" aria-label="Email Address">

Testing: 

inspekt axe --level 21aa
# Look for "label" violations

docs.title: 4. Keyboard Navigation
docs.text:
The problem: Interactive elements can't be accessed via keyboard.

Why it matters: Users who can't use a mouse are excluded.

Requirements: - All interactive elements must be focusable (Tab key) - Focus order must be logical - Visible focus indicator required - No keyboard traps (can Tab out)

How to fix: 

<!-- Bad - div is not keyboard accessible -->
<div onclick="handleClick()">Click me</div>

<!-- Good - button is keyboard accessible -->
<button onclick="handleClick()">Click me</button>

<!-- Good - div made accessible with role and tabindex -->
<div role="button" tabindex="0" onclick="handleClick()" onkeypress="handleClick()">
  Click me
</div>

CSS for focus indicators: 

/* Don't do this! */
*:focus {
  outline: none; /* ❌ Removes focus indicator */
}

/* Do this instead */
button:focus,
a:focus {
  outline: 2px solid #0066CC;
  outline-offset: 2px;
}

Manual testing: 

# Automated test
inspekt axe --level 21aa

# Manual keyboard test
# 1. Close your mouse/trackpad
# 2. Navigate page using only Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, Arrow keys
# 3. Verify you can reach all interactive elements
# 4. Verify you can see where focus is
# 5. Verify you can't get stuck (keyboard trap)

docs.title: 5. Heading Hierarchy
docs.text:
The problem: Heading levels skip (H1 → H3) or are out of order.

Why it matters: Screen readers use headings for navigation. Logical structure is essential.

How to fix: 

<!-- Bad - skips H2 -->
<h1>Main Page Title</h1>
<h3>Subsection</h3>  <!-- Skipped H2! -->

<!-- Good - logical hierarchy -->
<h1>Main Page Title</h1>
<h2>Major Section</h2>
<h3>Subsection</h3>
<h3>Another Subsection</h3>
<h2>Another Major Section</h2>

Rules: - One H1 per page (page title) - Don't skip levels (H1 → H3) - Headings should describe content - Visual styling ≠ heading level (use CSS)

Testing: 

# View heading structure
inspekt outline

# Check for heading-order violations
inspekt axe --level 21aa --tags best-practice

docs.title: 6. ARIA Usage
docs.text:
The problem: ARIA attributes used incorrectly or unnecessarily.

Why it matters: Broken ARIA is worse than no ARIA.

First rule of ARIA: Don't use ARIA.

Use semantic HTML instead: 

<!-- Bad - unnecessary ARIA -->
<div role="button" tabindex="0" aria-pressed="false">Click</div>

<!-- Good - semantic HTML -->
<button>Click</button>

When ARIA is needed: 

<!-- Good - Live region for dynamic updates -->
<div role="alert" aria-live="polite">
  Form submitted successfully!
</div>

<!-- Good - Expanded state for accordion -->
<button aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="panel">
  Show Details
</button>
<div id="panel" hidden>
  Details here...
</div>

Testing: 

inspekt axe --level 21aa
# Look for ARIA-related violations

# Create git hook: .git/hooks/pre-commit
#!/bin/bash

echo "Running accessibility audit..."

inspekt open http://localhost:3000 --wait
RESULT=$(inspekt axe --level 21aa --json)

CRITICAL=$(echo "$RESULT" | jq '.summary.criticalCount')
SERIOUS=$(echo "$RESULT" | jq '.summary.seriousCount')

if [ "$CRITICAL" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "❌ Critical accessibility issues found! Fix before committing."
    exit 1
fi

if [ "$SERIOUS" -gt 5 ]; then
    echo "⚠️  Warning: $SERIOUS serious accessibility issues"
fi

echo "✅ Accessibility check passed"
exit 0

docs.text:
# .github/workflows/accessibility.yml
name: Accessibility Testing

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  a11y-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2

      - name: Install Inspekt
        run: pip install inspekt

      - name: Start servers
        run: |
          inspekt server start
          npm run dev &
          sleep 5

      - name: Run accessibility audit
        run: |
          inspekt open http://localhost:3000 --wait
          inspekt axe --level 21aa --json > results.json

      - name: Check results
        run: |
          CRITICAL=$(jq '.summary.criticalCount' results.json)
          SERIOUS=$(jq '.summary.seriousCount' results.json)

          if [ "$CRITICAL" -gt 0 ] || [ "$SERIOUS" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "❌ Accessibility violations found!"
            echo "Critical: $CRITICAL, Serious: $SERIOUS"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Upload results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v2
        with:
          name: accessibility-results
          path: results.json

docs.title: Manual Testing Checklist
docs.text:
Automated tools catch ~30-40% of issues. Also test manually:

Keyboard navigation: - [ ] Tab through all interactive elements - [ ] Verify visible focus indicators - [ ] Test modals/dialogs (can you escape?) - [ ] Test dropdown menus - [ ] Test custom widgets

Screen reader testing: - [ ] Test with NVDA (Windows, free) - [ ] Test with JAWS (Windows, paid) - [ ] Test with VoiceOver (Mac, built-in) - [ ] Verify all images have meaningful alt text - [ ] Verify form labels are announced - [ ] Verify error messages are announced - [ ] Test landmark navigation

Visual testing: - [ ] Zoom to 200% (text should reflow) - [ ] Test high contrast mode - [ ] Test with color blindness simulation - [ ] Verify color is not the only indicator

Mobile testing: - [ ] Test with screen reader on mobile - [ ] Verify touch targets are 44×44 pixels minimum - [ ] Test with zoom enabled - [ ] Verify orientation (portrait/landscape)

Track accessibility over time:

#!/bin/bash
# Save baseline
inspekt axe --json > baseline.json

# After changes
inspekt axe --json > current.json

# Compare
BASELINE_VIOLATIONS=$(jq '.summary.violationCount' baseline.json)
CURRENT_VIOLATIONS=$(jq '.summary.violationCount' current.json)

if [ "$CURRENT_VIOLATIONS" -gt "$BASELINE_VIOLATIONS" ]; then
  echo "❌ Accessibility regression detected!"
  echo "Was: $BASELINE_VIOLATIONS, Now: $CURRENT_VIOLATIONS"
  exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash
PAGES=(
  "/"
  "/about"
  "/products"
  "/contact"
  "/blog"
)

for page in "${PAGES[@]}"; do
  echo "Testing $page..."
  inspekt open "https://example.com$page" --wait
  inspekt axe --level 21aa --json > "audit-${page//\//-}.json"

# Summary report
echo "Page,Violations,Critical,Serious" > summary.csv
for file in audit-*.json; do
  PAGE=$(echo "$file" | sed 's/audit-//;s/.json//')
  TOTAL=$(jq '.summary.violationCount' "$file")
  CRITICAL=$(jq '.summary.criticalCount' "$file")
  SERIOUS=$(jq '.summary.seriousCount' "$file")
  echo "$PAGE,$TOTAL,$CRITICAL,$SERIOUS" >> summary.csv
done

cat summary.csv

docs.title: ✅ Do
docs.text:
• Test early and often during development
  • Fix critical and serious issues immediately
  • Test with real screen readers, not just automated tools
  • Test keyboard navigation manually
  • Include accessibility in code review
  • Document accessibility standards for your team
  • Test authenticated and dynamic states
  • Track accessibility metrics over time

docs.title: ❌ Don't
docs.text:
• Rely solely on automated testing (catches ~35% of issues)
  • Ignore "incomplete" checks (need manual review)
  • Use ARIA when semantic HTML suffices
  • Remove focus indicators (:focus outline)
  • Use color alone to convey information
  • Skip manual keyboard testing
  • Forget to test with zoom enabled
  • Assume your site is accessible without testing

Add these to your .bashrc or .zshrc:

# Quick page title
zt() {

# Quick URL

  inspekt links --only-urls

zcount() {
  local selector="${1:-.item}"

zwatch() {

docs.title: Retry Logic
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash

retry_command() {
  local max_attempts=3
  local attempt=1
  local delay=2

  while [ $attempt -le $max_attempts ]; do
    echo "Attempt $attempt/$max_attempts..."

    if "$@"; then
      return 0
    fi

    if [ $attempt -lt $max_attempts ]; then
      echo "Failed. Retrying in ${delay}s..."
      sleep $delay
      delay=$((delay * 2))
    fi

    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
  done

  echo "All attempts failed" >&2
  return 1
}

# Usage
retry_command inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.dynamic-content').textContent"

#!/bin/bash

# Extract data from multiple pages in parallel
urls=(
  "https://example.com/page1"
  "https://example.com/page2"

)

pids=()

for url in "${urls[@]}"; do
  (

    title=$(inspekt eval "document.title" --format raw)
    links=$(inspekt links --only-urls | wc -l)
    echo "$url,$title,$links" >> results.csv
  ) &

done

# Wait for all to complete

done

#!/bin/bash
# Scrape product data from multiple pages

output_file="products.jsonl"
base_url="https://example.com/products"
total_pages=5

> "$output_file"  # Clear file

for page in $(seq 1 $total_pages); do
  echo "Scraping page $page/$total_pages..."

  # Navigate

  # Wait for products to load
  inspekt wait ".product" --visible

  # Extract data

    Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.product')).map(p => ({
      name: p.querySelector('.product-name')?.textContent.trim(),
      price: p.querySelector('.product-price')?.textContent.trim(),
      rating: p.querySelector('.rating')?.textContent.trim(),
      image: p.querySelector('img')?.src,
      url: p.querySelector('a')?.href
    }))
  " --format json | jq -c '.[]' >> "$output_file"

  echo "Page $page complete"

done

echo "Scraping complete. Total products: $(wc -l < "$output_file")"

#!/bin/bash
# Monitor page for changes and alert

url="https://example.com/status"
selector=".status-indicator"
check_interval=300  # 5 minutes
last_status=""

echo "Monitoring: $url"
echo "Selector: $selector"
echo "Interval: ${check_interval}s"

while true; do
  # Navigate and extract status
  inspekt open "$url" --wait
  current_status=$(inspekt eval "document.querySelector('$selector').textContent" --format raw)

  # Check for changes
  if [ -n "$last_status" ] && [ "$current_status" != "$last_status" ]; then
    echo "Status changed: $last_status → $current_status"

    # Send alert (macOS)
    osascript -e "display notification \"Status: $current_status\" with title \"Page Monitor\""

    # Or send email
    # echo "Status changed to: $current_status" | mail -s "Alert" user@example.com
  fi

  last_status="$current_status"
  echo "$(date): $current_status"

  sleep "$check_interval"
done

#!/bin/bash

echo "Running browser tests..."

# Start server if not running
if ! inspekt server status &>/dev/null; then

  sleep 2

#!/bin/bash

cache_dir="$HOME/.zen-cache"
cache_ttl=300  # 5 minutes

mkdir -p "$cache_dir"

get_cached_or_fetch() {
  local key="$1"
  local command="$2"
  local cache_file="$cache_dir/$(echo "$key" | md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1)"

  # Check cache
  if [ -f "$cache_file" ]; then
    age=$(($(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "$cache_file")))
    if [ $age -lt $cache_ttl ]; then
      cat "$cache_file"
      return 0
    fi
  fi

  # Fetch and cache
  result=$(eval "$command")
  echo "$result" > "$cache_file"
  echo "$result"
}

# Usage
title=$(get_cached_or_fetch "page-title" "inspekt eval 'document.title' --format raw")

docs.title: 1. Use Specific Selectors
docs.text:
# Good
inspekt click "#submit-btn"
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.product[data-id=\"123\"]')"

# Avoid
inspekt click "button"
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('div div div button')"

docs.title: 2. Handle Errors Gracefully
docs.text:
# Good
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.optional')?.textContent || 'Not found'"

# Avoid (may crash)
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.optional').textContent"

docs.title: 3. Batch Related Operations
docs.text:
# Good - single command
inspekt eval "({title: document.title, links: document.links.length})"

# Avoid - multiple commands
# inspekt eval "document.title"
# inspekt eval "document.links.length"

docs.title: 4. Use Appropriate Timeouts
docs.text:
# Quick operations
inspekt eval "document.title" --timeout 5

# Slow operations
inspekt eval "await fetch('/api/data').then(r => r.json())" --timeout 30

docs.title: 5. Test in Different Browsers
docs.text: Different browsers have different behaviors. Test your scripts in: - Chrome/Chromium - Firefox - Safari - Edge

docs.title: Command Hangs
docs.text:
# Reduce timeout
inspekt eval "document.title" --timeout 5

# Check for infinite loops
inspekt eval "console.log('test'); document.title"

docs.title: High Memory Usage
docs.text:
# Limit results
inspekt eval "Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.item')).slice(0, 100)"

# Clear caches periodically
rm -rf "$HOME/.zen-cache"/*

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
# Add delays between requests
for url in "${urls[@]}"; do
  inspekt open "$url" --wait
  inspekt eval "document.title"
  sleep 2  # Be polite
done

docs.title: AI Features
docs.text: Master AI-powered features in Inspekt. Learn how to generate article summaries, create page descriptions for accessibility, and configure AI integration with mods.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Inspekt integrates with AI through mods to provide two powerful features:

  • inspekt summarize - Generate concise article summaries
  • inspekt describe - Create accessible page descriptions for screen readers

Both commands extract page content and use AI to generate natural-language output.

docs.title: Install mods
docs.text:
AI features require mods to be installed:

# macOS/Linux
brew install charmbracelet/tap/mods

# Or with go
go install github.com/charmbracelet/mods@latest

docs.title: Configure mods
docs.text:
On first run, mods will prompt you to configure an AI provider:

mods

Supported providers: - OpenAI (GPT-3.5, GPT-4) - Anthropic (Claude) - Ollama (local models) - Azure OpenAI - And more...

Set your API key:

# OpenAI
export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-key-here"

# Anthropic
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="your-key-here"

# Or configure via mods
mods --settings

docs.title: Article Summarization
docs.text: The inspekt summarize command extracts article content and generates a concise summary.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
inspekt summarize

Example output: 

This article discusses the importance of web accessibility and provides
practical techniques for making websites more inclusive. Key points include
semantic HTML, ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, and screen reader compatibility.
The author emphasizes that accessibility benefits all users, not just those with
disabilities, by improving usability and SEO.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Extract Article - Uses Mozilla Readability to extract main content
  2. Detect Language - Automatically detects page language
  3. Generate Summary - Sends content to AI via mods
  4. Return Result - Displays concise summary

docs.title: Show Full Article
docs.text:
inspekt summarize --format full

Displays the extracted article content without summarizing:

Title: Web Accessibility Best Practices
Author: John Doe
Published: 2024-01-15

Web accessibility is crucial for creating inclusive digital experiences...
[Full extracted article text]

docs.title: Language Control
docs.text:
Override the output language:

# Summarize in French
inspekt summarize --language fr
inspekt summarize --lang fr

# Summarize in Spanish
inspekt summarize --language es

# Summarize in German
inspekt summarize --lang de

docs.title: Language Detection Flow
docs.text:
1. CLI flag (--language) - Highest priority
  2. Config file (ai-language setting) - Second priority
  3. Page language (HTML lang attribute) - Third priority
  4. Let AI decide - Default behavior

docs.title: Debug Mode
docs.text:
See the full prompt sent to AI:

inspekt summarize --debug

Output: 

=== PROMPT ===
Please summarize the following article in 2-3 sentences.
Respond in English.

Title: Web Accessibility Best Practices
Content: [article content]
=== END PROMPT ===

Useful for: - Understanding what's sent to AI - Debugging language issues - Customizing prompts

docs.title: Custom Prompts
docs.text:
Edit the summarization prompt:

# Edit prompt file
nano ~/zen_bridge/prompts/summary.prompt

Default prompt: 

Please summarize the following article in 2-3 concise sentences.
Focus on the main points and key takeaways.

{LANGUAGE_INSTRUCTION}

Title: {TITLE}
Content: {CONTENT}

Variables: - {LANGUAGE_INSTRUCTION} - Injected when --language is used - {TITLE} - Article title - {CONTENT} - Extracted article text

docs.title: Page Descriptions for Screen Readers
docs.text: The inspekt describe command generates natural-language page descriptions perfect for blind users.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
inspekt describe

Example output: 

This webpage is in Dutch, but is also available in English and French.
At the top you can navigate to services, articles, careers, about us
and contact us. The main part contains a rather long article about an
empathy lab with five headings. The footer contains standard links
such as a sitemap and privacy statement.

docs.title: What It Analyzes
docs.text:
The describe command extracts:

  • Available languages - Alternate language versions
  • Navigation menus - Main navigation structure
  • Page landmarks - Headers, main content, footer, etc.
  • Heading structure - H1-H6 hierarchy and count
  • Main content type - Article, form, list, etc.
  • Content length - Approximate reading time
  • Significant images - Alt text and image count
  • Forms - Input fields and their purposes
  • Footer utilities - Links like privacy policy, sitemap

docs.title: Language Control
docs.text:
# Describe in French
inspekt describe --language fr

# Describe in Spanish
inspekt describe --lang es

docs.title: Debug Mode
docs.text:
inspekt describe --debug

See the extracted page structure and full prompt.

docs.title: Custom Prompts
docs.text:
Edit the description prompt:

nano ~/zen_bridge/prompts/describe.prompt

Default prompt: 

Create a concise description of this webpage for a blind user using a screen reader.
Focus on:
- Available languages
- Navigation structure
- Main content type and purpose
- Interactive elements
- Overall page organization

Keep it natural and conversational.

{LANGUAGE_INSTRUCTION}

Page Structure:
{PAGE_STRUCTURE}

docs.title: Language Settings
docs.text:
Set default AI output language in config.json:

{
  "ai-language": "en"
}

Supported languages: - en - English - es - Spanish - fr - French - de - German - nl - Dutch - it - Italian - pt - Portuguese - ja - Japanese - zh - Chinese - And more...

docs.text:
Configure mods behavior:

mods --settings

# Use specific model
mods --model gpt-4

docs.title: Content Curation
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash
# Batch summarize articles

URLS=(
  "https://example.com/article1"
  "https://example.com/article2"
  "https://example.com/article3"
)

for url in "${URLS[@]}"; do
  echo "=== $url ===" >> summaries.txt
  inspekt open "$url" --wait
  inspekt summarize >> summaries.txt
  echo "" >> summaries.txt
done

docs.title: Documentation Assistant
docs.text:
