docs.text: Command Purpose Example inspekt click "selector" Click element inspekt click "#submit" inspekt double-click "selector" Double-click inspekt double-click ".file" inspekt right-click "selector" Right-click inspekt right-click ".context" inspekt wait "selector" Wait for element inspekt wait ".modal" --visible inspekt send "text" Type text inspekt send "hello" --selector "#input" inspekt inspect "selector" Inspect element inspekt inspect "h1" inspekt inspected Get inspected details inspekt inspected inspekt highlight "selector" Highlight elements inspekt highlight "a" --color blue inspekt screenshot --selector Screenshot element inspekt screenshot --selector "h1"

docs.title: JavaScript Execution
docs.text: Master JavaScript execution in Inspekt. Learn inline code execution, file execution, stdin piping, timeout handling, error handling, output formatting, and advanced patterns.

docs.title: Execution Methods
docs.text: Inspekt offers three ways to execute JavaScript code in your browser.

docs.title: 1. Inline Code Execution
docs.text:
Execute code directly from the command line:

inspekt eval "document.title"

Best for: - Quick one-liners - Testing expressions - Shell scripts with short code snippets

docs.title: 2. File Execution
docs.text:
Execute code from JavaScript files:

inspekt eval --file script.js
# or
inspekt exec script.js

Best for: - Complex scripts - Reusable code - Version-controlled automation

docs.title: 3. stdin Piping
docs.text:
Pipe code from stdin:

cat script.js | inspekt eval
echo "document.title" | inspekt eval

Best for: - Generated code - Dynamic scripts - Shell pipelines

docs.title: Simple Expressions
docs.text:
# Get page title
inspekt eval "document.title"

# Get URL
inspekt eval "window.location.href"

# Count elements
inspekt eval "document.querySelectorAll('a').length"

# Check if element exists
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.modal') !== null"

docs.title: Complex Expressions
docs.text:
# Array operations
inspekt eval "Array.from(document.links).map(a => a.href)"

# Object literals (wrap in parentheses)
inspekt eval "({title: document.title, url: location.href})"

# Filter and map
inspekt eval "Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('img')).filter(img => img.alt).map(img => img.src)"

# Reduce
inspekt eval "Array.from(document.links).reduce((acc, link) => acc + link.textContent.length, 0)"

docs.title: Multi-line Code
docs.text:
Use newlines and proper JavaScript syntax:

inspekt eval "
  const products = document.querySelectorAll('.product');
  const data = Array.from(products).map(p => ({
    name: p.querySelector('.name').textContent,
    price: p.querySelector('.price').textContent
  }));
  return data;
"

Multi-line Tips

  • Separate statements with semicolons
  • Use return for the final value
  • Proper indentation makes code readable

docs.title: Handling Quotes
docs.text:
Shell quoting can be tricky. Here are the rules:

# Double quotes - escape inner double quotes
inspekt eval "document.querySelector(\"h1\").textContent"

# Single quotes in double quotes - no escaping needed
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('h1').textContent"

# Backticks for template literals - use single quotes outside
inspekt eval 'document.querySelector("h1").textContent = `Hello ${name}`'

# Heredoc for complex quoting
inspekt eval <<'EOF'
const selector = 'div[data-value="complex"]';
const element = document.querySelector(selector);
return element?.textContent;
EOF

docs.title: Basic File Execution
docs.text:
script.js: 

// Extract all links
const links = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a'));
return links.map(link => ({
  text: link.textContent.trim(),
  href: link.href,
  external: link.hostname !== location.hostname
}));

Execute: 

inspekt exec script.js
# or
inspekt eval --file script.js

docs.title: File with Modules
docs.text:
Modern JavaScript syntax is supported:

extract-data.js: 

// Extract product data with validation
const products = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.product'));

function extractProduct(element) {
  const name = element.querySelector('.product-name')?.textContent?.trim();
  const price = element.querySelector('.product-price')?.textContent?.trim();
  const image = element.querySelector('.product-image')?.src;

  // Validate required fields
  if (!name || !price) return null;

  return { name, price, image };
}

const data = products.map(extractProduct).filter(Boolean);

return {
  count: data.length,
  products: data,
  extracted: new Date().toISOString()
};

docs.title: Built-in Scripts
docs.text:
Inspekt includes several ready-to-use scripts in the zen/scripts/ directory:

# Extract all images
inspekt exec zen/scripts/extract_images.js

# Extract table data
inspekt exec zen/scripts/extract_table.js

# Get SEO metadata
inspekt exec zen/scripts/extract_metadata.js

# Performance metrics
inspekt exec zen/scripts/performance_metrics.js

# Inject jQuery
inspekt exec zen/scripts/inject_jquery.js

# Highlight elements
inspekt exec zen/scripts/highlight_selector.js

docs.title: Creating Your Own Scripts
docs.text:
1. Create a script directory: 

mkdir -p ~/zen-scripts

2. Write your script: 

// ~/zen-scripts/extract-prices.js
const prices = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.price'));
return prices.map(p => ({
  text: p.textContent,
  value: parseFloat(p.textContent.replace(/[^0-9.]/g, ''))
}));

3. Execute: 

inspekt exec ~/zen-scripts/extract-prices.js --format json

docs.title: Pipe from Files
docs.text: cat script.js | inspekt eval

docs.title: Pipe from echo
docs.text: echo "document.title" | inspekt eval

docs.title: Generate Code Dynamically
docs.text:
# Generate selector from variable
SELECTOR=".product"
echo "document.querySelectorAll('$SELECTOR').length" | inspekt eval

# Generate complex code
cat <<EOF | inspekt eval
const selector = '$SELECTOR';
const elements = document.querySelectorAll(selector);
return Array.from(elements).length;
EOF

docs.title: Pipe Chains
docs.text:
# Extract, filter, execute
grep -v "^//" script.js | inspekt eval

# Combine multiple commands
echo "document.links.length" | inspekt eval | awk '{print "Found " $1 " links"}'

docs.title: Default Timeout
docs.text:
Commands timeout after 10 seconds by default:

inspekt eval "document.title"  # 10 second timeout

docs.title: Custom Timeout
docs.text:
Adjust for slow operations:

# 30 second timeout
inspekt eval "await fetch('/api/data').then(r => r.json())" --timeout 30

# 5 second timeout (strict)
inspekt eval "document.title" --timeout 5

# 60 second timeout (very slow operations)
inspekt eval "await heavyComputation()" --timeout 60

docs.title: Timeout Examples
docs.text:
Long-running API call: 

inspekt eval "
  const response = await fetch('/api/large-dataset');
  const data = await response.json();
  return data.items.length;
" --timeout 30

Wait for lazy-loaded content: 

inspekt eval "
  // Scroll to load content
  for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    window.scrollTo(0, document.body.scrollHeight);
    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1000));
  }
  return document.querySelectorAll('.lazy-item').length;
" --timeout 30

docs.title: Timeout Errors
docs.text:
When a timeout occurs:

Error: Request timed out after 10 seconds

Solutions: 1. Increase timeout with --timeout 2. Optimize your JavaScript code 3. Break into smaller operations 4. Check for infinite loops

docs.title: JavaScript Errors
docs.text:
Runtime errors are caught and displayed:

inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.missing').click()"

Output: 

TypeError: Cannot read property 'click' of null
  at <eval>:1:42

docs.title: Syntax Errors
docs.text:
Invalid JavaScript is caught:

inspekt eval "document..title"

Output: 

SyntaxError: Unexpected token '.'

docs.title: Handling Errors in Your Code
docs.text:
Use try-catch for graceful error handling:

inspekt eval "
  try {
    const element = document.querySelector('.maybe-exists');
    return element.textContent;
  } catch (error) {
    return null;
  }
"

docs.title: Defensive Coding
docs.text:
Use optional chaining and nullish coalescing:

# Optional chaining
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.modal')?.textContent"

# Nullish coalescing
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.price')?.textContent ?? 'N/A'"

# Combined
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.product')?.querySelector('.price')?.textContent ?? 'No price'"

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Validate before operating:

inspekt eval "
  const element = document.querySelector('.submit-btn');
  if (!element) {
    return { error: 'Button not found' };
  }
  element.click();
  return { success: true };
"

docs.title: Format Options
docs.text:
Control output format with the --format flag:

Format Description Use Case auto Smart formatting (default) General use json Valid JSON Scripting, piping to jq raw Plain text Shell variables

docs.title: Auto Format (Default)
docs.text:
Intelligently formats output:

inspekt eval "document.title"
# Output: Example Domain (plain text)

inspekt eval "({title: document.title, url: location.href})"
# Output: Pretty-printed JSON

docs.title: JSON Format
docs.text:
Always outputs valid JSON:

inspekt eval "document.title" --format json
# Output: "Example Domain"

inspekt eval "({title: document.title, links: document.links.length})" --format json
# Output: {"title":"Example Domain","links":15}

Perfect for jq: 

inspekt eval "({title: document.title, url: location.href})" --format json | jq '.title'
# Output: "Example Domain"

docs.title: Raw Format
docs.text:
No formatting - just the value:

inspekt eval "document.title" --format raw
# Output: Example Domain

inspekt eval "document.links.length" --format raw
# Output: 15

Perfect for shell variables: 

TITLE=$(inspekt eval "document.title" --format raw)
COUNT=$(inspekt eval "document.links.length" --format raw)
echo "$COUNT links on $TITLE"

docs.title: Metadata Flags
docs.text:
Add context to output:

# Add URL
inspekt eval "document.title" --url

# Add title
inspekt eval "document.links.length" --title

# Add both
inspekt eval "document.links.length" --url --title

Output: 

URL: https://example.com
Title: Example Domain

15

docs.title: Async/Await
docs.text:
Full support for promises and async/await:

# Fetch API
inspekt eval "await fetch('/api/data').then(r => r.json())"

# Multiple awaits
inspekt eval "
  const response = await fetch('/api/users');
  const users = await response.json();
  return users.length;
"

# Promise.all
inspekt eval "
  const promises = Array.from({length: 5}, (_, i) =>
    fetch(\`/api/item/\${i}\`).then(r => r.json())
  );
  return await Promise.all(promises);
"

docs.title: Working with Arrays
docs.text:
# Map
inspekt eval "Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a')).map(a => a.href)"

# Filter
inspekt eval "Array.from(document.links).filter(a => a.hostname === location.hostname)"

# Reduce
inspekt eval "Array.from(document.images).reduce((sum, img) => sum + img.naturalWidth, 0)"

# Find
inspekt eval "Array.from(document.links).find(a => a.textContent.includes('Contact'))"

# Some/Every
inspekt eval "Array.from(document.images).every(img => img.alt)"

docs.title: Working with Objects
docs.text:
# Object.keys
inspekt eval "Object.keys(window)"

# Object.entries
inspekt eval "Object.entries(localStorage).map(([k,v]) => ({key: k, value: v}))"

# Destructuring
inspekt eval "
  const {title, URL: url} = document;
  return {title, url};
"

docs.title: DOM Traversal
docs.text:
# Parent
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.child').parentElement.tagName"

# Children
inspekt eval "Array.from(document.body.children).map(el => el.tagName)"

# Siblings
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('h1').nextElementSibling?.tagName"

# Closest
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.nested').closest('.container')?.className"

docs.title: Performance Optimization
docs.text:
Cache selectors: 

inspekt eval "
  const products = document.querySelectorAll('.product');
  return Array.from(products).map(p => {
    // Reuse 'p' instead of querying again
    return {
      name: p.querySelector('.name').textContent,
      price: p.querySelector('.price').textContent
    };
  });
"

Use document fragments: 

inspekt eval "
  const fragment = document.createDocumentFragment();
  for (let i = 0; i < 100; i++) {
    const div = document.createElement('div');
    div.textContent = i;
    fragment.appendChild(div);
  }
  document.body.appendChild(fragment);
  return 'Added 100 divs efficiently';
"

docs.title: Data Transformation
docs.text:
CSV Generation: 

inspekt eval "
  const rows = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('table tr'));
  return rows.map(row =>
    Array.from(row.cells).map(cell => cell.textContent).join(',')
  ).join('\n');
" --format raw > data.csv

JSON Transformation: 

inspekt eval "
  const links = Array.from(document.links);
  return links.reduce((acc, link) => {
    acc[link.textContent] = link.href;
    return acc;
  }, {});
" --format json

docs.title: State Management
docs.text:
Store data globally: 

# Set
inspekt eval "window.zenData = {extracted: Date.now(), items: [1,2,3]}"

# Get
inspekt eval "window.zenData"

# Update
inspekt eval "window.zenData.items.push(4); window.zenData"

docs.title: Console Integration
docs.text:
# Log to browser console
inspekt eval "console.log('Debug:', document.title); document.title"

# Console table
inspekt eval "
  const data = Array.from(document.links).slice(0, 5).map(a => ({
    text: a.textContent,
    href: a.href
  }));
  console.table(data);
  return data.length;
"

# Console time
inspekt eval "
  console.time('query');
  const result = document.querySelectorAll('*').length;
  console.timeEnd('query');
  return result;
"

docs.title: Browser APIs
docs.text:
Local Storage: 

inspekt eval "localStorage.getItem('token')"
inspekt eval "localStorage.setItem('key', 'value')"
inspekt eval "Object.keys(localStorage)"

Cookies: 

inspekt eval "document.cookie"
inspekt eval "document.cookie.split(';').length"

Performance API: 

inspekt eval "performance.now()"
inspekt eval "performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize"
inspekt eval "performance.timing.loadEventEnd - performance.timing.navigationStart"

Clipboard API: 

inspekt eval "await navigator.clipboard.readText()"
inspekt eval "await navigator.clipboard.writeText('Hello from CLI')"

docs.title: 1. Return Structured Data
docs.text:
# Good - structured return
inspekt eval "
  return {
    success: true,
    count: document.links.length,
    timestamp: Date.now()
  };
"

# Avoid - multiple console.logs
inspekt eval "
  console.log('Links:', document.links.length);
  console.log('Images:', document.images.length);
"

docs.title: 2. Use Meaningful Variable Names
docs.text:
# Good
inspekt eval "
  const productElements = document.querySelectorAll('.product');
  const productData = Array.from(productElements).map(extractProductInfo);
  return productData;
"

# Avoid
inspekt eval "
  const a = document.querySelectorAll('.product');
  const b = Array.from(a).map(c => extractProductInfo(c));
  return b;
"

docs.title: 3. Handle Edge Cases
docs.text:
inspekt eval "
  const element = document.querySelector('.may-not-exist');
  if (!element) {
    return { error: 'Element not found' };
  }
  return { text: element.textContent };
"

docs.title: 4. Comment Complex Code
docs.text:
inspekt eval "
  // Extract all external links
  const allLinks = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a'));

  // Filter to external only
  const externalLinks = allLinks.filter(link =>
    link.hostname !== location.hostname && link.hostname !== ''
  );

  // Return count and sample
  return {
    total: externalLinks.length,
    sample: externalLinks.slice(0, 5).map(l => l.href)
  };
"

docs.title: 5. Use Functions for Reusability
docs.text:
script.js: 

function extractProductData(selector) {
  const products = document.querySelectorAll(selector);
  return Array.from(products).map(product => ({
    name: product.querySelector('.name')?.textContent?.trim(),
    price: product.querySelector('.price')?.textContent?.trim(),
    available: !product.classList.contains('out-of-stock')
  })).filter(p => p.name && p.price);
}

return extractProductData('.product-item');

docs.title: 1. Use Browser DevTools
docs.text: Open browser console while running commands to see: - console.log() output - JavaScript errors with stack traces - Network requests - Performance metrics

docs.title: 2. Test in REPL First
docs.text:
inspekt repl
zen> document.querySelector('.complex-selector')
zen> Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.items')).length
zen> exit

docs.title: 3. Break Down Complex Code
docs.text:
# Step 1: Test selector
inspekt eval "document.querySelectorAll('.product').length"

# Step 2: Test extraction
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.product .name').textContent"

# Step 3: Combine
inspekt eval "Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.product')).map(p => p.querySelector('.name').textContent)"

docs.title: 4. Add Debug Output
docs.text:
inspekt eval "
  console.log('Starting extraction...');
  const products = document.querySelectorAll('.product');
  console.log('Found products:', products.length);
  const data = Array.from(products).map(p => {
    const name = p.querySelector('.name')?.textContent;
    console.log('Extracted:', name);
    return {name};
  });
  console.log('Complete:', data.length);
  return data;
"

docs.title: 1. Forgetting to Return
docs.text:
# Wrong - no return
inspekt eval "
  const links = document.querySelectorAll('a');
  links.length;
"
# Output: undefined

# Correct
inspekt eval "
  const links = document.querySelectorAll('a');
  return links.length;
"
# Output: 15

docs.title: 2. Async Without Await
docs.text:
# Wrong - returns Promise
inspekt eval "fetch('/api/data').then(r => r.json())"
# Output: [object Promise]

# Correct - await the promise
inspekt eval "await fetch('/api/data').then(r => r.json())"
# Output: {data: [...]}

docs.title: 3. Quoting Issues
docs.text:
# Wrong - quote mismatch
inspekt eval 'document.querySelector("div[data-id="123"]")'

# Correct - escape or use heredoc
inspekt eval "document.querySelector(\"div[data-id='123']\")"

docs.title: 4. Not Checking Null
docs.text:
# Wrong - may throw error
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.missing').click()"

# Correct - check first
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.missing')?.click() ?? 'Element not found'"

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Element Interaction - Click, inspect, and interact with elements
  • Data Extraction - Extract structured data
  • Advanced Usage - Complex patterns and scripting

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Welcome to Inspekt - a powerful CLI tool that lets you control your browser from the command line. Execute JavaScript, automate tasks, extract data, and interact with web pages without leaving your terminal.

docs.title: What is Inspekt?
docs.text:
Inspekt is a command-line interface that connects your terminal to your web browser through a WebSocket-based architecture. It allows you to:

  • Execute JavaScript code in your active browser tab
  • Interact with page elements (click, inspect, highlight, wait)
  • Extract data (links, images, tables, metadata)
  • Automate form filling and navigation
  • Debug and test web applications
  • Monitor browser activity in real-time
  • Control your browser entirely from your keyboard

Think of it as a bridge between your terminal and your browser - hence the name.

docs.title: 1. CLI Tool (Your Terminal)
docs.text:
When you run commands like inspekt eval "document.title", the CLI tool:

  • Parses your command and options
  • Formats the JavaScript code
  • Sends an HTTP request to the local server
  • Waits for the response
  • Displays the result

docs.title: 2. Bridge Server (Background Process)
docs.text:
The server acts as a message broker:

  • Listens for HTTP requests from the CLI (port 8765)
  • Maintains WebSocket connections with browser tabs (port 8766)
  • Routes commands to the active browser tab
  • Returns results back to the CLI
  • Runs in the background as a daemon

Start the server with: 

inspekt server start --daemon

docs.title: 3. Browser Userscript (In Your Browser)
docs.text:
A lightweight userscript runs in your browser:

  • Establishes a WebSocket connection to the server
  • Receives JavaScript code from the server
  • Executes the code in the page context
  • Sends results back to the server
  • Works across page navigations

The userscript must be installed in a userscript manager like Violentmonkey or Tampermonkey.

docs.title: Why WebSockets?
docs.text:
Traditional HTTP polling would be slow and inefficient. WebSockets provide:

  • Instant communication - No polling delays
  • Bi-directional - Server can push to browser, browser can push to server
  • Persistent connection - One connection serves multiple commands
  • Low overhead - Minimal latency compared to HTTP requests

docs.title: Message Flow Example
docs.text:
When you run inspekt eval "document.title":

  1. CLI → Server (HTTP) 

    POST http://127.0.0.1:8765/execute
{
  "code": "document.title",
  "timeout": 10
}

  2. Server → Browser (WebSocket) 

    {
  "type": "execute",
  "code": "document.title",
  "id": "req-123"
}

  3. Browser executes code and responds (WebSocket) 

    {
  "type": "response",
  "id": "req-123",
  "result": "Example Domain",
  "ok": true
}

  4. Server → CLI (HTTP Response) 

    {
  "ok": true,
  "result": "Example Domain"
}

  5. CLI displays output 

    Example Domain

docs.title: Security Considerations
docs.text:
The WebSocket connection is local only:

  • Server binds to 127.0.0.1 (localhost)
  • Not accessible from external networks
  • No authentication needed (local-only access)
  • Userscript only connects to localhost

This means Inspekt can only control browsers on your own machine.

docs.title: When to Use Inspekt
docs.text: Inspekt is ideal for:

docs.title: Web Development & Debugging
docs.text:
• Inspect application state (window.myApp, Redux stores)
  • Test JavaScript functions interactively
  • Debug DOM manipulations
  • Monitor performance metrics
  • Inject jQuery or other libraries for testing

docs.title: Web Scraping & Data Extraction
docs.text:
• Extract data from authenticated pages (logged-in dashboards)
  • Scrape tables, lists, and structured data
  • Download files (images, PDFs, videos)
  • Extract metadata (Open Graph, Twitter Cards)
  • Monitor page changes over time

docs.title: Browser Automation
docs.text:
• Fill and submit forms
  • Navigate through multi-page workflows
  • Click buttons and interact with elements
  • Wait for dynamic content to load
  • Automate repetitive tasks

docs.title: Accessibility Testing
docs.text:
• Run WCAG compliance audits (inspekt axe)
  • Check heading structure (inspekt outline)
  • Find images without alt text
  • Test keyboard navigation (inspekt control)
  • Generate page descriptions for screen readers

docs.title: Content Analysis
docs.text:
• Generate AI summaries of articles (inspekt summarize)
  • Get concise page descriptions (inspekt describe)
  • Analyze link structures
  • Check SEO metadata

docs.title: Shell Scripting & CI/CD
docs.text:
• Integrate browser data into shell scripts
  • Monitor build dashboards
  • Automate visual regression testing
  • Extract data for reports

docs.title: When NOT to Use Inspekt
docs.text: Inspekt is not suitable for:

docs.title: Heavy Automation at Scale
docs.text:
• Use Playwright or Puppeteer for:
  • Running hundreds of parallel browser instances
  • Server-side rendering testing
  • Complex test suites with retries and parallelization

docs.title: Distributed/Remote Automation
docs.text:
• Inspekt only works on localhost
  • For remote browser control, use Playwright, Puppeteer, or Selenium Grid

docs.title: Production Monitoring
docs.text:
• Don't rely on Inspekt for production monitoring
  • Use proper APM tools (Datadog, New Relic, etc.)

docs.title: Privacy-Sensitive Operations
docs.text:
• Inspekt has access to everything in your browser
  • Don't use it on pages with sensitive credentials
  • Be careful with commands that extract cookies or local storage

docs.title: Execute JavaScript
docs.text:
Run any JavaScript code in your browser:

inspekt eval "document.title"
inspekt eval "Array.from(document.links).map(a => a.href)"
inspekt eval "({url: location.href, title: document.title})" --format json

docs.title: Interactive REPL
docs.text:
Live JavaScript session:

inspekt repl
zen> document.querySelectorAll('p').length
2
zen> exit

docs.title: Element Interaction
docs.text:
Click, inspect, highlight, and wait for elements:

inspekt click "button#submit"
inspekt inspect "h1"
inspekt highlight ".error" --color red
inspekt wait ".modal" --visible

docs.title: Data Extraction
docs.text:
Extract structured data:

inspekt links --only-external
inspekt outline
inspekt download
inspekt info --extended

docs.title: Accessibility Testing
docs.text:
Run comprehensive WCAG audits:

inspekt axe --level 21aa
inspekt axe --tags best-practice --json

docs.title: AI-Powered Features
docs.text:
Summarize and describe pages:

inspekt summarize
inspekt describe

Requires mods for AI integration.

docs.title: Keyboard Control
docs.text:
Navigate entirely from your keyboard:

inspekt control
# Use Tab, Enter, Arrow keys to navigate
# Press 'q' to quit

docs.title: Real-Time Monitoring
docs.text:
Watch browser activity:

inspekt watch input  # Monitor keyboard input
inspekt watch all    # Monitor all interactions

docs.title: Architecture Benefits
docs.text:
Inspekt follows a hexagonal architecture with clear separation of concerns:

  • Domain Layer - Pure business logic with Pydantic models
  • Adapter Layer - I/O operations (filesystem, WebSocket)
  • Service Layer - Application services and orchestration
  • Application Layer - CLI commands and server

This design ensures:

  • High testability (97%+ coverage on services)
  • Clear dependencies (no circular imports)
  • Easy extensibility (add new commands/services)
  • Maintainable codebase

See Architecture Guide for technical details.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Ready to try Inspekt? Check out these guides:

  1. Basic Commands - Start here for essential commands
  2. JavaScript Execution - Master code execution
  3. Element Interaction - Click, inspect, and interact
  4. Data Extraction - Extract structured data
  5. Accessibility Testing - WCAG compliance audits with axe-core
  6. AI Features - AI-powered summarization and descriptions
  7. Control Mode - Keyboard-only navigation
  8. Advanced Usage - Scripting and best practices

docs.text:
1. Install Inspekt and the userscript (see Installation guide)
  2. Start the server: inspekt server start --daemon
  3. Try basic commands: inspekt eval "document.title"
  4. Explore the guides above
  5. Check out the API Reference for complete documentation

docs.title: Getting Help
docs.text:
• Run inspekt --help to see all commands
  • Run inspekt <command> --help for command-specific help
  • Check the GitHub Issues for known issues
  • Read the Contributing Guide to contribute

Welcome to Inspekt - control your browser from the command line!

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text: Manage and run custom JavaScript plugins (bookmarklets) from the CLI, API, MCP, or web dashboard. Plugins let you save reusable code snippets that execute in your browser context.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Inspekt Plugins transform bookmarklets and custom JavaScript into managed, reusable tools that you can:

  • Run from CLI: inspekt plugin run my-plugin
  • Expose as MCP tools: Let AI agents execute your plugins
  • Manage via web dashboard: Edit, test, and organize with a full-featured code editor
  • Import/Export: Share plugins between machines or with colleagues

docs.title: Run a Plugin
docs.text:
# List all plugins
inspekt plugin list

# Run a plugin by name or ID
inspekt plugin run "Text Spacing"

# Run with JSON output
inspekt plugin run accessibility-checker --json

docs.title: Manage via Web Dashboard
docs.text:
# Open the plugins dashboard
inspekt plugins
# Or navigate to: http://localhost:8765/plugins

docs.title: From the Web Dashboard
docs.text:
1. Click Add Plugin in the header
  2. Choose your import method:
  3. From Bookmarklet URL: Paste a javascript:... URL
  4. Paste Code: Enter raw JavaScript directly
  5. Give your plugin a name and click Add Plugin

docs.title: From a Bookmarklet URL
docs.text:
This is the easiest way to import existing bookmarklets you've collected.

What is a bookmarklet?

A bookmarklet is a browser bookmark that contains JavaScript code instead of a URL. They start with javascript: and are typically URL-encoded.

Example bookmarklet URL: 

javascript:(function()%7Balert(%22Hello%22)%7D)()

How to import:

  1. Copy the bookmarklet URL from your browser's bookmark bar (right-click > Edit > copy the URL)
  2. In the Add Plugin modal, select "From Bookmarklet URL"
  3. Paste the URL into the "Bookmarklet URL" field
  4. Enter a descriptive name
  5. Click "Add Plugin"

What happens behind the scenes:

  1. The javascript: prefix is stripped
  2. The code is URL-decoded (e.g., %7B becomes {)
  3. The code is optionally prettified for readability
  4. A new plugin is created with the clean JavaScript

Before: 

javascript:(function()%7Bvar%20d%3Ddocument%2Cs%3Dd.createElement(%27style%27)%3Bs.textContent%3D%27*%7Bline-height%3A1.5%21important%7D%27%3Bd.head.appendChild(s)%7D)()

After: 

(function () {
  var d = document,
    s = d.createElement('style');
  s.textContent = '* { line-height: 1.5 !important }';
  d.head.appendChild(s);
})();

docs.title: From Raw Code
docs.text:
If you have JavaScript code (not a bookmarklet URL), use the "Paste Code" tab:

// Extract all headings
(function() {
  const headings = document.querySelectorAll('h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6');
  return Array.from(headings).map(h => ({
    level: h.tagName,
    text: h.textContent.trim()
  }));
})();

docs.title: Via CLI
docs.text:
# Create from code
inspekt plugin create "My Plugin" --code "(function() { alert('hello'); })()"

# Create from file
inspekt plugin create "My Plugin" --file script.js

docs.title: Via API
docs.text:
# Create from bookmarklet
curl -X POST http://localhost:8765/api/plugins/from-bookmarklet \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Text Spacing",
    "bookmarklet": "javascript:(function()%7Balert(%22hello%22)%7D)()"
  }'

# Create from code
curl -X POST http://localhost:8765/api/plugins \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "My Plugin",
    "code": "(function() { return document.title; })()"
  }'

docs.title: Plugin Properties
docs.text: Property Description Name Display name for the plugin Category Optional grouping (e.g., "a11y", "utility", "dev") Description What the plugin does Credits Original author, source URL, license info Code The JavaScript to execute Returns Data Whether the plugin returns a value MCP Exposed Make available as an MCP tool for AI agents Unload Behavior How to reverse the plugin's effects

docs.title: Unload Behavior
docs.text: Some plugins inject styles or modify the DOM. The unload feature lets you reverse these changes.

docs.title: Unload Modes
docs.text: Mode Description Use Case Toggle Run the same code again to unload Self-toggling plugins (e.g., dark mode) Custom Run separate unload code When reversal needs different logic Not Reversible No unload support One-time actions (e.g., form submission)

docs.title: Example: Toggle Mode
docs.text:
A plugin that adds then removes a CSS class:

(function() {
  document.body.classList.toggle('debug-mode');
})();

First run adds the class, second run removes it.

docs.title: Example: Custom Unload Code
docs.text:
Main code: 

(function() {
  const style = document.createElement('style');
  style.id = 'my-plugin-styles';
  style.textContent = '* { outline: 1px solid red !important }';
  document.head.appendChild(style);
})();

Unload code: 

(function() {
  const style = document.getElementById('my-plugin-styles');
  if (style) style.remove();
})();

docs.title: Unload via CLI
docs.text:
# Unload a plugin
inspekt plugin unload "Text Spacing"

docs.title: MCP Integration
docs.text: Expose plugins as MCP tools that AI agents can use.

docs.title: Enable MCP for a Plugin
docs.text:
1. Edit the plugin in the web dashboard
  2. Check "Expose as MCP tool"
  3. Save the plugin

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
When MCP is enabled, the plugin becomes available as an MCP tool:

mcp__inspekt__run_plugin_{slug}

For example, a plugin named "Text Spacing" becomes:

mcp__inspekt__run_plugin_text_spacing

docs.title: AI Agent Usage
docs.text:
AI agents can then call your plugin:

Use the text spacing plugin to improve readability on this page.

The agent will call mcp__inspekt__run_plugin_text_spacing and execute your code in the browser.

docs.title: Code Editor
docs.text:
The built-in CodeMirror 6 editor provides:

  • Syntax highlighting for JavaScript
  • Syntax error detection with inline markers
  • Format button - Prettify code with Prettier
  • Copy button - Copy code to clipboard
  • Fullscreen mode - Press Escape to exit

docs.title: Test Execution
docs.text:
Click Test to run the plugin in your current browser tab. The console panel shows:

  • Console output (log, warn, error, info)
  • Return values
  • Execution time

docs.title: Import/Export
docs.text:
Export: Click Export to download all plugins as JSON.

Import: Click Import to upload a JSON file. Choose how to handle conflicts:

  • Skip existing: Don't overwrite existing plugins
  • Replace existing: Overwrite plugins with same ID

docs.title: CLI Commands
docs.text:
# List all plugins
inspekt plugin list
inspekt plugin list --json

# Show plugin details
inspekt plugin show <name-or-id>

# Run a plugin
inspekt plugin run <name-or-id>
inspekt plugin run <name-or-id> --json

# Unload a plugin (if supported)
inspekt plugin unload <name-or-id>

# Create a plugin
inspekt plugin create "Name" --code "..."
inspekt plugin create "Name" --file script.js

# Delete a plugin
inspekt plugin delete <name-or-id>

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text: Method Endpoint Description GET /api/plugins List all plugins POST /api/plugins Create plugin from code POST /api/plugins/from-bookmarklet Create from bookmarklet URL GET /api/plugins/{id} Get plugin details PUT /api/plugins/{id} Update plugin DELETE /api/plugins/{id} Delete plugin POST /api/plugins/{id}/run Execute plugin POST /api/plugins/{id}/unload Unload plugin POST /api/plugins/test Test code without saving GET /api/plugins/export Export all as JSON POST /api/plugins/import Import from JSON

docs.title: Accessibility: Text Spacing
docs.text:
WCAG 2.1 text spacing test:

(function () {
  const style = document.createElement('style');
  style.id = 'wcag-text-spacing';
  style.textContent = `
    * {
      line-height: 1.5 !important;
      letter-spacing: 0.12em !important;
      word-spacing: 0.16em !important;
    }
    p { margin-bottom: 2em !important; }
  `;
  document.head.appendChild(style);
})();

docs.title: Utility: Show All Images
docs.text:
Display all images with their alt text:

(function () {
  const images = document.querySelectorAll('img');
  return Array.from(images).map(img => ({
    src: img.src,
    alt: img.alt || '(no alt)',
    width: img.naturalWidth,
    height: img.naturalHeight
  }));
})();

docs.title: Debug: Highlight Focus
docs.text:
Show focus indicator on all focusable elements:

(function () {
  const style = document.createElement('style');
  style.textContent = `
    :focus {
      outline: 3px solid #f00 !important;
      outline-offset: 2px !important;
    }
  `;
  document.head.appendChild(style);
})();

docs.title: 1. Use IIFEs
docs.text:
Wrap code in Immediately Invoked Function Expressions to avoid polluting the global scope:

(function () {
  // Your code here
})();

docs.title: 2. Return Structured Data
docs.text:
When extracting data, return structured objects:

(function () {
  return {
    title: document.title,
    url: location.href,
    linkCount: document.links.length
  };
})();

docs.title: 3. Add Cleanup IDs
docs.text:
When injecting elements, use IDs for easy removal:

// Inject
const style = document.createElement('style');
style.id = 'my-unique-plugin-id';
document.head.appendChild(style);

// Remove later
document.getElementById('my-unique-plugin-id')?.remove();

docs.title: 4. Handle Missing Elements
docs.text:
Use optional chaining and nullish coalescing:

const text = document.querySelector('.may-not-exist')?.textContent ?? 'Not found';

docs.title: 5. Document Your Plugins
docs.text:
Use the Credits field to note:

  • Original author or source
  • License information
  • Related documentation links

docs.title: Plugin Doesn't Run
docs.text:
1. Check browser console for JavaScript errors
  2. Verify the server is running (inspekt status)
  3. Test the code in the web dashboard first

docs.title: Bookmarklet Import Fails
docs.text:
1. Ensure the URL starts with javascript:
  2. Check for proper URL encoding
  3. Try pasting the decoded code directly

docs.title: MCP Tools Not Appearing

docs.title: Recording and Replaying Browser Interactions
docs.text: This tutorial walks you through Inspekt's powerful recording and replay feature. You'll learn how to capture user interactions, add assertions for testing, and automate repetitive tasks.

docs.title: What You'll Learn
docs.text:
• Record browser interactions to a YAML file
  • Understand the recording file format
  • Edit recordings to add assertions
  • Replay recordings for automated testing
  • Create accessibility test suites
  • Build regression tests for your workflows

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before starting, make sure you have:

  1. Inspekt installed - See Installation Guide
  2. Browser extension installed - See Browser Extensions
  3. Bridge server running - Start with inspekt start

Verify your setup:

inspekt status
# Should show: Bridge server is running

docs.title: Step 1: Open a Page
docs.text:
Let's record a simple interaction. First, open a website in your browser:

inspekt open https://example.com

Or navigate manually to any page in your browser.

docs.title: Step 2: Start Recording
docs.text:
inspekt record my-first-recording.yaml

You'll see:

Recording: https://example.com
Press Ctrl+C to stop and save

docs.title: Step 3: Interact with the Page
docs.text:
Now interact with the page normally:

  • Click on links and buttons
  • Type in form fields
  • Press Tab to navigate
  • Hover over menus

Each action appears in real-time:

  click: a "More information..."
  navigate: https://www.iana.org/help/example-domains
  click: #search-input "Search"
  type: #search-input (6 chars)
  keypress: Enter

docs.title: Step 4: Stop and Save
docs.text:
Press Ctrl+C to stop recording:

Stopping recording...

Recording saved to: my-first-recording.yaml
Duration: 23.5s | Steps: 8

docs.title: Step 5: View Your Recording
docs.text:
Open the YAML file to see what was captured:

cat my-first-recording.yaml

# Inspekt Recording v1.0
# Generated: 2025-12-02T14:30:00+00:00
# Duration: 23.5s
# URL: https://example.com

metadata:
  version: "1.0"
  created_at: "2025-12-02T14:30:00+00:00"
  duration_ms: 23500
  starting_url: "https://example.com"
  viewport:
    width: 1920
    height: 1080
  zoom: 1.0

steps:
  - timestamp: 0
    action: navigate
    url: "https://example.com"

  - timestamp: 2340
    action: click
    target:
      selector: "a"
      fallback_selectors:
        - "body > div > p:nth-of-type(2) > a"
      text: "More information..."
      accessible_name: "More information..."
      tag: a
    position:
      x: 245
      y: 367

  - timestamp: 4521
    action: navigate
    url: "https://www.iana.org/help/example-domains"

  # ... more steps

docs.title: Metadata Section
docs.text:
Every recording starts with metadata:

metadata:
  version: "1.0"              # Recording format version
  created_at: "2025-12-02..." # When recorded
  duration_ms: 23500          # Total duration
  starting_url: "https://..." # Starting page
  viewport:
    width: 1920               # Browser width
    height: 1080              # Browser height
  zoom: 1.0                   # Zoom level

docs.title: Navigate
docs.text:
URL changes (including SPA navigation):

- timestamp: 0
  action: navigate
  url: "https://example.com/page"

docs.title: Click
docs.text:
Mouse clicks with element targeting:

- timestamp: 1234
  action: click
  target:
    selector: "#submit-btn"
    fallback_selectors:
      - "[data-testid='submit']"
      - "form > button"
    text: "Submit"
    accessible_name: "Submit form"
    tag: button
  position:
    x: 450
    y: 320

docs.title: Type
docs.text:
Text input into fields:

- timestamp: 2500
  action: type
  target:
    selector: "#email"
    accessible_name: "Email address"
  value: "user@example.com"

For password fields, values are masked:

- timestamp: 3000
  action: type
  target:
    selector: "#password"
  value: "••••••••"
  sensitive: true

docs.title: Keypress
docs.text:
Special keys and keyboard shortcuts:

- timestamp: 3500
  action: keypress
  key: "Tab"
  modifiers: []

# With modifiers
- timestamp: 4000
  action: keypress
  key: "s"
  modifiers:
    - ctrl

docs.title: Hover
docs.text:
Mouse hover on interactive elements:

- timestamp: 5000
  action: hover
  target:
    selector: "nav .dropdown"
    accessible_name: "Menu"

docs.title: Target Object
docs.text:
The target object identifies elements:

target:
  selector: "#main-btn"           # Primary CSS selector
  fallback_selectors:             # Backup selectors (tried in order)
    - "[data-testid='main']"
    - "button.primary"
  text: "Click me"                # Visible text
  accessible_name: "Main action"  # ARIA accessible name
  tag: button                     # HTML tag
  role: button                    # ARIA role

Selector Priority (from most to least stable):

  1. ID: #element-id
  2. Test ID: [data-testid="..."]
  3. ARIA label: [aria-label="..."]
  4. Name attribute: input[name="..."]
  5. CSS path: div > form > button

docs.title: Shadow DOM Support
docs.text:
Inspekt has full support for Web Components with Shadow DOM. When you interact with elements inside a Shadow DOM, Inspekt automatically:

  1. Records the actual target - Uses event.composedPath() to capture the real element you clicked, not the outer custom element
  2. Generates piercing selectors - Creates special selectors that can traverse Shadow DOM boundaries
  3. Stores Shadow DOM metadata - Records both the shadow host and the inner selector

docs.title: Shadow DOM Recording Format
docs.text:
When you click on an element inside a Shadow DOM, the recording includes extra fields:

- timestamp: 2500
  action: click
  target:
    selector: "#tag_2"                                    # Inner element selector
    shadow_host: "#odp-search--122343"                    # The custom element host
    piercing_selector: "#odp-search--122343 >>> #tag_2"  # Full path through Shadow DOM
    text: null
    tag: select

The >>> delimiter indicates a Shadow DOM boundary. During replay, Inspekt:

  1. First tries the piercing_selector to navigate directly to the element
  2. Falls back to shadow_host + selector combination
  3. If those fail, recursively searches through all Shadow roots on the page

docs.title: Example: Web Component Interaction
docs.text:
A page with a custom search component:

<odp-search id="search-widget">
  #shadow-root (open)
    <select id="category">
      <option>Category 1</option>
      <option>Category 2</option>
    </select>
    <input type="text" id="query">
    <button id="search-btn">Search</button>
</odp-search>

Recording interactions with this component:

# Select from dropdown inside Shadow DOM
- timestamp: 1000
  action: click
  target:
    selector: "#category"
    shadow_host: "#search-widget"
    piercing_selector: "#search-widget >>> #category"
    tag: select

# Type in the search box
- timestamp: 2000
  action: type
  target:
    selector: "#query"
    shadow_host: "#search-widget"
    piercing_selector: "#search-widget >>> #query"
  value: "example search"

# Click the search button
- timestamp: 3000
  action: click
  target:
    selector: "#search-btn"
    shadow_host: "#search-widget"
    piercing_selector: "#search-widget >>> #search-btn"
    accessible_name: "Search"
    tag: button

docs.title: Nested Shadow DOM
docs.text:
Inspekt supports multiple levels of Shadow DOM nesting. The piercing selector uses multiple >>> delimiters:

piercing_selector: "#outer-component >>> #inner-component >>> #button"

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Closed Shadow DOM: Elements in closed Shadow roots (mode: 'closed') cannot be accessed or recorded
  • Dynamic Shadow DOM: Elements created after page load are found via fallback search

docs.title: Part 3: Adding Assertions
docs.text: Assertions turn recordings into tests. Edit your YAML file to add expect: fields.

docs.title: Visibility Assertions
docs.text:
Check if elements are visible after an action:

- timestamp: 5500
  action: click
  target:
    selector: "#login-btn"
  expect:
    visible: ".welcome-message"   # Should appear
    hidden: ".login-form"         # Should disappear

docs.title: URL Assertions
docs.text:
Verify navigation:

- timestamp: 5500
  action: click
  target:
    selector: "#login-btn"
  expect:
    url_contains: "/dashboard"

docs.title: Text Assertions
docs.text:
Check for text content:

- timestamp: 6000
  action: navigate
  url: "https://example.com/success"
  expect:
    text_contains: "Thank you for your order"

docs.title: Console Error Checks
docs.text:
Add an inspekt command to check for JavaScript errors:

- timestamp: 7000
  action: inspekt
  command: "console --level error"
  expect:
    empty: true    # No console errors

docs.title: Accessibility Checks
docs.text:
Add accessibility testing at key points:

- timestamp: 8000
  action: inspekt
  command: "axe --level 2aa"
  expect:
    violations: 0  # No WCAG 2.1 AA violations

docs.title: Element State Assertions
docs.text:
Check form field states:

- timestamp: 4000
  action: click
  target:
    selector: "#accept-terms"
  expect:
    checked: "#accept-terms"       # Checkbox should be checked
    enabled: "#submit-btn"         # Submit button should be enabled

- timestamp: 5000
  action: type
  target:
    selector: "#email"
  value: "test@example.com"
  expect:
    value: "#email"
    value_equals: "test@example.com"

docs.title: Wait/Retry for Async Content
docs.text:
For dynamic content that takes time to appear:

- timestamp: 6000
  action: click
  target:
    selector: "#submit-btn"
  expect:
    visible: ".success-message"
    hidden: ".loading-spinner"
    wait: 5000                    # Wait up to 5 seconds
    retry: 100                    # Check every 100ms

docs.title: Conditional Actions
docs.text:
Skip steps based on page state:

# Skip cookie banner if already dismissed
- timestamp: 500
  action: click
  target:
    selector: "#accept-cookies"
  skip_if:
    hidden: "#cookie-banner"

Wait for conditions before executing:

# Wait for form to load before typing
- timestamp: 1000
  action: type
  target:
    selector: "#email"
  value: "user@example.com"
  wait_for:
    visible: "#email"
    timeout: 5000

docs.title: Basic Replay
docs.text:
inspekt replay my-first-recording.yaml

Output:

Replaying: my-first-recording.yaml
URL: https://example.com
Steps: 8 of 8

  [1] navigate → https://example.com OK
  [2] click → a "More information..." OK
  [3] navigate → https://www.iana.org/help/example-domains OK
  [4] click → #search-input "Search" OK
  [5] type → #search-input (6 chars) OK
  [6] keypress → Enter OK
  [7] navigate → https://www.iana.org/search?q=example OK
  [8] click → .result-item OK

──────────────────────────────────────────────────
✓ All 8 steps passed
  Duration: 5.2s

docs.title: Replay Options
docs.text:
By default, replay uses real-time timing - it matches the original pace of your recording.

# Real-time replay (default - matches original timing)
inspekt replay recording.yaml

# 2x speed (faster)
inspekt replay recording.yaml --speed 2

# Half speed (for debugging)
inspekt replay recording.yaml --slow

# Instant execution (skip all delays)
inspekt replay recording.yaml --instant

# Preview without executing
inspekt replay recording.yaml --dry-run

# Detailed output
inspekt replay recording.yaml --verbose

# Run only steps 3-6
inspekt replay recording.yaml --start-step 3 --end-step 6

# Disable visual/audio feedback (for CI environments)
inspekt replay recording.yaml --no-feedback

# Disable audio only (for shared workspaces)
inspekt replay recording.yaml --no-audio

docs.title: Visual and Audio Feedback
docs.text:
By default, replay includes visual and audio feedback:

  • Visual indicators - Pulsing circle shows click targets, typing indicator for text input
  • Audio cues - Subtle sounds for clicks, typing, navigation, and errors

To disable for CI/CD or headless environments:

inspekt replay test.yaml --no-feedback      # Disable all
inspekt replay test.yaml --no-audio         # Audio only
inspekt replay test.yaml --no-visual        # Visual only

docs.title: Handling Failures
docs.text:
Replay continues on failure and reports all issues at the end:

Replaying: checkout.yaml
URL: https://shop.example.com
Steps: 12 of 12

  [1] navigate → https://shop.example.com OK
  [2] click → .product "Widget Pro" OK
  [3] click → #add-to-cart "Add to Cart" OK
  [4] click → #cart-icon OK
  [5] click → #checkout "Checkout" FAIL
  [6] type → #email (15 chars) OK
  ...

──────────────────────────────────────────────────
✗ 2 of 12 steps failed
  Passed: 10 | Failed: 2 | Skipped: 0
  Duration: 8.5s

Failures:

  Step 5: click
    Selector: #checkout
    Error: Element not found: #checkout

  Step 9: click
    Selector: #confirm
    Error: Assertion failed
    - Expected element to be visible: .order-confirmation

docs.title: Example 1: Login Flow Test
docs.text:
Record the login:

inspekt record login-test.yaml

# 2. Enter username
# 3. Enter password
# 4. Click login
# 5. Verify dashboard loads
# Press Ctrl+C

Edit to add assertions:

metadata:
  version: "1.0"
  starting_url: "https://app.example.com/login"
  # ...

steps:
  - timestamp: 0
    action: navigate
    url: "https://app.example.com/login"

  - timestamp: 1000
    action: click
    target:
      selector: "#username"

  - timestamp: 1500

Run the test:

Test that form validation works correctly:

docs.title: Recording Tips
docs.text:
1. Start fresh - Begin from a known state (logged out, empty cart, etc.)

  2. Keep it focused - One workflow per recording

  3. Use stable selectors - Prefer IDs and data-testid attributes

  4. Skip hover for tests - Unless testing hover behavior specifically 

    inspekt record --no-hover stable-test.yaml

  5. Name files descriptively 

    login-success.yaml
login-invalid-password.yaml
checkout-guest-user.yaml
checkout-returning-customer.yaml

docs.title: Editing Tips
docs.text:
1. Always add assertions - A recording without assertions isn't a test

  2. Test the happy path AND error cases

  3. Add accessibility checks at key interactions

  4. Handle passwords securely

  5. Replace •••••••• with actual values (don't commit to git)

  6. Or use environment variables in a wrapper script

  7. Remove unnecessary steps - Delete accidental clicks, redundant navigation

docs.title: Replay Tips
docs.text:
1. Use dry-run first 

    inspekt replay test.yaml --dry-run

  2. Debug with verbose and slow speed 

    inspekt replay test.yaml --verbose --speed 0.5

  3. Test specific sections 

    inspekt replay test.yaml --start-step 5 --end-step 10

  4. Use appropriate speed for CI 

    inspekt replay test.yaml --speed 2 --step-delay 200

docs.title: Basic Shell Script
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash
# run-tests.sh

set -e  # Exit on first failure

echo "Starting Inspekt tests..."

# Ensure server is running
inspekt start

# Wait for server
sleep 2

# Run all test recordings
FAILED=0
for file in tests/*.yaml; do
    echo ""
    echo "Running: $file"
    if inspekt replay "$file" --speed 2; then
        echo "✓ Passed: $file"
    else
        echo "✗ Failed: $file"
        FAILED=1
    fi
done

# Report results
echo ""
if [ $FAILED -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "All tests passed!"
    exit 0
else
    echo "Some tests failed!"
    exit 1
fi

docs.title: GitHub Actions Example
docs.text:
# .github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml
name: E2E Tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'

      - name: Install Inspekt
        run: pip install inspekt

      - name: Setup Chrome
        uses: browser-actions/setup-chrome@v1

      - name: Start Inspekt
        run: |
          inspekt start &
          sleep 3

      - name: Run E2E Tests
        run: |
          for file in tests/e2e/*.yaml; do
            inspekt replay "$file" --speed 2
          done

docs.title: "Element not found"
docs.text:
Cause: Selector doesn't match any element

Solutions: 1. Check if the page structure changed 2. Update the selector in your YAML 3. Add more fallback selectors 4. Ensure you're on the right page first

docs.title: "Cannot replay masked password"
docs.text:
Cause: Password was masked during recording

Solution: Edit the YAML and replace •••••••• with the actual password

docs.title: "Assertion failed"
docs.text:
Cause: Expected condition not met

Solutions: 1. Verify the expected behavior is correct 2. Add delay before the assertion (increase --step-delay) 3. Check for timing issues with dynamic content

docs.title: Recording is flaky
docs.text: Solutions: 1. Use --no-hover to skip hover events 2. Add explicit waits with increased --step-delay 3. Use stable selectors (IDs, data-testid) 4. Record from a consistent starting state

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
You've learned how to:

  • ✅ Record browser interactions with inspekt record
  • ✅ Understand the YAML recording format
  • ✅ Add assertions for testing
  • ✅ Replay recordings with inspekt replay
  • ✅ Create accessibility test suites
  • ✅ Integrate with CI/CD pipelines

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Read the inspekt record reference
  • Read the inspekt replay reference
  • Learn about accessibility testing
  • Explore advanced usage patterns

docs.title: Troubleshooting CSP Issues
docs.text: This guide helps you understand and troubleshoot Content Security Policy (CSP) issues with Inspekt.

docs.title: What is CSP?
docs.text:
Content Security Policy (CSP) is a security feature that websites use to control what resources (scripts, styles, connections) can be loaded and executed on their pages.

CSP is implemented through HTTP headers or <meta> tags and acts as a protective barrier against: - Cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks - Data injection attacks - Unauthorized script execution - Unwanted network connections

docs.title: Why Inspekt May Not Work
docs.text: Inspekt requires two things that CSP can block:

docs.title: 1. JavaScript Execution
docs.text: When you run commands like inspekt eval "document.title", Zen injects JavaScript into the page. Strict CSP policies may block this.

docs.title: 2. WebSocket Connection
docs.text: The userscript connects to ws://localhost:8766 to communicate with the Zen CLI. CSP's connect-src directive can block connections to localhost.

docs.title: In Browser Console
docs.text:
Open your browser's DevTools (F12) and look for errors like:

Refused to connect to 'ws://localhost:8766' because it violates the
following Content Security Policy directive: "connect-src 'self'"

docs.title: Inspekt Warning
docs.text:
Starting with version 3.5, Inspekt automatically detects CSP and shows a warning:

⚠️ Inspekt: CSP Detected

This website has Content Security Policy (CSP) restrictions that block Inspekt.

What this means:
• WebSocket connections to localhost are blocked
• Zen commands will not work on this page

Why this happens:
• High-security sites (GitHub, banking, government) use CSP
• CSP prevents unauthorized scripts and connections
• This is a security feature, not a bug

docs.title: Manual Check
docs.text:
Check if a site has CSP using curl:

curl -I https://example.com | grep -i content-security

Example output: 

Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://api.example.com

This policy blocks WebSocket connections to localhost.

docs.title: High-Security Sites (Usually Blocked)
docs.text:
Sites with strict CSP that typically block Inspekt:

  • Code Hosting: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket
  • Google Services: Gmail, Drive, Docs, Cloud Console
  • Financial: Banking websites, payment processors
  • Government: Government portals, public services
  • Enterprise: Corporate intranals, cloud platforms (AWS, Azure)
  • Security-Focused: Password managers, VPN services

docs.title: Sites That Usually Work
docs.text:
• News websites (most)
  • Blogs and personal sites
  • Documentation sites
  • E-commerce (many)
  • Social media (some)
  • Local development servers

docs.title: ✅ Test on Different Sites
docs.text:
The simplest solution is to use Inspekt on sites without strict CSP:

# Works on most sites
inspekt eval "document.title"

# Try different domains
inspekt eval "window.location.href"

docs.title: ✅ Verify Server is Running
docs.text:
Sometimes the issue isn't CSP:

# Check if server is running
inspekt server status

# Restart if needed
inspekt server restart

docs.title: ✅ Check Browser Console
docs.text:
Always check the browser console for specific error messages:

  1. Open DevTools (F12)
  2. Go to Console tab
  3. Look for Inspekt messages or CSP violations
  4. Share error messages when reporting issues

docs.title: ❌ What Won't Work
docs.text:
These approaches do not work and are not recommended:

  1. Disabling CSP in browser - Removes all security, very dangerous
  2. Modifying HTTP headers - Requires browser extension with elevated privileges
  3. Proxying through another domain - CSP still blocks injected scripts

docs.title: Future Solutions
docs.text: We're exploring ways to make Inspekt work with CSP:

docs.title: Browser Extension (Future)
docs.text:
A full browser extension (not just a userscript) could: - Use chrome.tabs.executeScript() API with CSP bypass - Maintain WebSocket connections with elevated privileges - Require installation from Chrome/Firefox store

Trade-offs: - More installation steps - Store review process - More restrictive permissions needed

docs.title: CSP-Compatible Mode (Future)
docs.text:
A limited mode that works within CSP constraints: - Read-only operations - No arbitrary script execution - Limited to predefined commands

Trade-offs: - Reduced functionality - No custom JavaScript evaluation - Limited use cases

docs.title: Reporting CSP Issues
docs.text:
If you encounter CSP issues on sites where you'd expect Zen to work:

  1. Check the browser console for specific CSP errors
  2. Note the website URL and any error messages
  3. Test on a different site to verify Zen works elsewhere
  4. Report the issue at: https://github.com/roelvangils/inspekt/issues

Include: - Website URL (if public) - CSP policy (from curl or browser) - Error messages from console - Inspekt version (inspekt --version)

docs.title: CSP Directives That Affect Zen
docs.text: Directive Impact Example Blocking Policy connect-src Blocks WebSocket connect-src 'self' script-src Blocks injected scripts script-src 'self' default-src Fallback for other directives default-src 'none'

docs.title: What Inspekt Needs
docs.text:
For Inspekt to work, the CSP must allow:

Content-Security-Policy:
  connect-src 'self' ws://localhost:8766 ws://127.0.0.1:8766;
  script-src 'self' 'unsafe-eval';

Most high-security sites will never allow this, by design.

docs.title: Detection Methods
docs.text:
Inspekt uses multiple methods to detect CSP:

  1. Meta tag detection: Checks for <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy">
  2. Connection failure patterns: Multiple failed WebSocket attempts
  3. Error message analysis: Catches CSP-related error messages

docs.title: GitHub (Strict CSP)
docs.text:
$ curl -I https://github.com | grep -i content-security
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; connect-src 'self' *.github.com

Result: ❌ Inspekt blocked (localhost not in connect-src)

docs.title: Personal Blog (No CSP)
docs.text:
$ curl -I https://example-blog.com | grep -i content-security
# No CSP header

Result: ✅ Inspekt works

docs.title: E-commerce Site (Moderate CSP)
docs.text:
$ curl -I https://shop.example.com | grep -i content-security
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https:

Result: ❌ Inspekt blocked (https: only, no ws://)

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Test before relying on Zen - Verify it works on your target sites
  2. Use for development - Works great on localhost and dev environments
  3. Report unexpected blocks - Help us improve CSP detection
  4. Stay informed - Watch for updates on CSP compatibility

docs.title: Why don't you just bypass CSP?
docs.text:
CSP is a critical security feature. Bypassing it would: - Require dangerous browser modifications - Compromise site security - Violate browser security policies - Put users at risk

Inspekt respects web security standards.

docs.title: Will this ever be fixed?
docs.text:
"Fixed" implies CSP is a bug - it's not. CSP is working as designed.

We're exploring alternatives like browser extensions, but these require different installation and permission models.

docs.title: Can I whitelist localhost in CSP?
docs.text:
Only site owners can modify their CSP policy. If you control the website, you can add:

Content-Security-Policy: connect-src 'self' ws://localhost:8766

But this only works for your own sites.

docs.title: Does this affect all userscripts?
docs.text:
CSP affects any tool that: - Injects scripts into pages - Makes external connections - Executes dynamic code

This is a common limitation of browser automation tools on high-security sites.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• CSP is a security feature, not a bug
  • High-security sites block Zen by design
  • Inspekt detects and warns about CSP (v3.5+)
  • Use Zen on sites without strict CSP
  • Report unexpected issues to help improve detection

For most use cases (development, testing, personal sites), Inspekt works great. For high-security production sites, CSP restrictions are intentional and appropriate.
